name = ancrel.9235.b.evopred

descriptions.zh:
我们行星表面的考察队报告了一些令人震惊的发现。这颗行星上有多个主要城市，所有城市均被遗弃，但就其年代而言，城市的状况相当良好。每座城市的基础设施和城市规划都格外精心而协调，表明这是一个内部有着极高凝聚力，有着浓厚集权、集体主义色彩的文明——或许甚至是某种类型的格式塔意识。

基于其建筑设计和内部设施，建造这一切的物种看起来属于小型真菌类生物，其技术先进程度相当低下。他们到底去了哪里仍然未知。
descriptions.en:
Our surface expedition has reported back some astounding findings. The planet has multiple major cities, all abandoned but in quite good shape considering their age. The infrastructure and urban planning of each city is remarkably structured and harmonious, indicating a highly cohesive civilization driven by centralized, collective ideals - perhaps even a gestalt consciousness of some kind.

Based on the architecture and interior fixtures, the species that built all this seems to have been small fungoids, with a fairly low state of technical advancement. Where exactly they all went remains unknown.

options.script:
name = DIG
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh: 对[From.Planet.GetName]上消失文明的进一步研究解答了一些问题，但同时也提出了更多问题。这些朴素，坚实的建筑物有着数千年的历史，看起来均大致在同一时间段建造，或许前后不超过一个世纪。与之相似的是，全行星范围内对城区建筑物的任何增建和翻修看起来也是间隔一段漫长的时间后突然开始进行。此社会发展不时中断的奇异现象似乎并未对人口规模产生可观的影响。
descriptions.en: Further studies of the lost civilization of [From.Planet.GetName] have given rise to more questions than answers. The plain, sturdy structures are thousands of years old, and all seem to have been constructed at roughly the same time, perhaps as brief as a single century. Similarly, any additions or renovations to the urban structure seemed to be done planet-wide at sudden, widely-separated intervals. The oddly-punctuated development of this society seems to show no appreciable change in population size.

options.script:
name = DIG
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
最近的研究成果为寻找[From.Planet.GetName]上神秘消失的城市建设者带来了一些启示。显然，这里的真菌物种有着集体死亡和重生的循环。整颗星球上，该物种的子实体几乎同时成熟，并成长为一个相互联系的蜂巢意识的一部分。在他们长达数百年的生命周期中，他们破土而出并重新启用了以前几代人所建造和抛弃的城市。

当下一次死亡/重生事件临近时，一种影响到所有个体的信号被释放出来。通过无性繁殖，他们产下一个埋在地下的子实体。亲代凋亡后，其躯体腐烂并为子实体周围的地面施肥。经过漫长的休眠期后，子实体成熟，循环重新开始。
descriptions.en:
A recent breakthrough shone some light on the vanished city builders of [From.Planet.GetName]. Apparently, the fungal species has a collective cycle of mass death and rebirth. They hatch en masse, almost simultaneously across the whole planet, and grow up as part of a linked hive mind collective. In the course of their hundreds of years long life cycle, they spread out and reclaim the cities built and abandoned by previous died-off generations.

When nearing the next death/rebirth event, they heed some species-wide biological clarion call. Through asexual reproduction they give birth to a pod that is buried in the ground. The parent dies, and the body decays and fertilizes the ground around the pod. After a long dormant period, the pods hatch, and the cycle begins anew.

options.script:
name = DIG
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
对[FromFrom.Planet.GetName]地面的发掘最终揭示了失踪人口的命运。他们一开始都在地下孕育着，成长着并准备破土而出。但当时一些自然现象——很可能是流星的影响，打乱了几十年里的天气和季节，破坏了该星球的生态系统。当他们破土而出时，这个世界已不适宜生存了。

那本应共同庆祝的重生很快便变成一场波及全部个体的饥饿，缓慢但不可缓和，最终导致整个物种的灭绝。
descriptions.en:
Soil excavations on [FromFrom.Planet.GetName] finally revealed the fate of the missing population. They were all in their gestation pod state in the ground, growing and getting ready to emerge, when some natural phenomenon - most likely a meteor impact that upset weather and seasons for a few decades - disrupted the planet's ecosystem. As they hatched they found a world devoid of sustenance.

What should have been shared, celebratory rebirth quickly turned into a slow, collective starvation - and ultimately the species' extinction.

descriptions.zh:
对该真菌物种的心理学和社会学研究给他们失踪之谜带来了令人不安的解答。在某些时候，这种有着蜂巢意识的物种开始质疑它们那永恒的，看似毫无意义的生命周期。虚无主义的种子在整个社会中成长，最终达到高潮并压过了他们的生存本能，使他们作出了极端行为。

一旦出现，哪怕只出现在一个个体身上，这种论调便通过蜂巢网络迅速影响到每一个个体，直到他们一致决定不再播下用于繁殖的子实体——并将它们付之一炬。
descriptions.en:
A speculative psychological and sociological investigation of the fungoid species' culture gave a disconcerting answer to the mystery of their disappearance. At some point the species as a whole started to question their perpetual, and seemingly pointless life cycle. A seed of existential nihilism grew in the entire population, culminating in a final act of defiance against their own survival instinct.

Once planted, perhaps even by a single being, this kernel of doubt spread with terrifying speed through the hive mind, until they decided in unison that the last crop of birth pods should not be planted - they should be burned.

descriptions.zh:
真菌社会消失之谜的谜底相当简单——该星球的居民从未离去。他们还在那里，在地下发育着。对一个暴露于地表的子实体的分析表明，该物种有着长达数百年的寿命。但相对于它们需要在地下发育的数千年，了了百载光阴不足为道。他们那长期以来被忽视的简陋城市依然静静矗立在那里，等待着他们的回归。

是的，他们都还在，在地下蛰伏，等待着重见天日，开始又一轮的生命循环。
descriptions.en:
The final answer to the mystery of the vanished fungoid society turned out to be fairly straightforward. The planet's population is not lost at all! They're still there, gestating underground. Analysis of an uncovered pod indicated that the species' centuries-long active lifespan was nothing compared to the pod-state gestation, which seems to go on for a few thousand years. Their simple cities, built to withstand long neglect, stand silently, awaiting their return.

So, there they all are, slumbering in the ground, awaiting the day when they'll rise and start the cycle once more.

descriptions.zh:
这些损毁严重，但又相当先进的建筑揭示出一个事实，这是一个即将步入太空航行领域的类人种族。翻译过来的文件记录以及大量的纪念建筑说明存在一个根深蒂固的宗教或者灵性信仰散布于整个文明之中。

§H伟大先驱§!这个词语反复被提及，看上去在这个社会中，这是一个神圣不可侵犯，需要敬畏的符号又或者概念。
descriptions.en:
Devastated, but fairly advanced, architecture hints at a technologically adept humanoid species on the verge of spacefaring capability. Translated documentation and extensive monumental architecture indicates a deeply seated religion or spirituality that permeated the entire civilization.

The phrase §HThe Grand Herald§! is mentioned repeatedly, and appears to be a figure or concept of divine awe and unquestioned reverence in this society.

options.script:
name = DIG
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
翻阅了在整颗星球上找到的浩如烟海的文件后——不得不说这个物种确实挺热爱书面语言——我们发现一个反复出现的概念十分显眼。其被描述为§H圣约预兆§!，是关于将要到来的世界末日的一些征兆，这引发了全体民众的多疑与恐慌。

由于这些宗教性的语言充满隐喻且晦涩难懂，我们难以搞清这个威胁的本质，但它对这个种族的心灵造成的影响却是实实在在的。他们开始集体向上天寻求神灵的帮助。
descriptions.en:
Sifting through the abundance of documentation found in the ruins across the planet - this species sure loved their written word - one recurring concept stands out. It's referred to as §HThe Testament of Omen§!, and it is some portent of impending doom that triggered paranoia and dread in the general population.

Due to the metaphorical and esoteric nature of the scriptural language, it's difficult to ascertain the true nature of this menace, but the effect on the psyche of the indigenous species is indisputable. En masse they seem to have looked to the heavens for divine intervention.

options.script:
name = DIG
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
建筑学分析师将那些在这个在文明消失前不久才建造好的建筑与其他建筑区分开来。这种风格的建筑遍布整颗星球：杂乱无章的实用主义建筑，专为重工业建造。不像老式居所，这些建筑从设计角度而言既朴实无华而又高度务实。也许是一种反传统的文化开始流行？

在每座建筑的入口上方写着§H奴役信条§!——对§H伟大先驱§!的一种祷告仪式以及它的神圣计划。理论认为，这是对§H圣约预兆§!中预言的末日的某种回应。
descriptions.en:
Architectural analysis has isolated the buildings that were assembled just before the civilization vanished. The pattern is the same across the planet: haphazard utilitarian constructs intended for heavy industrial work. Unlike older dwellings, these buildings are unadorned and noticeably pragmatic in their design. Perhaps a culture of iconoclasm took hold?

Over the entrance of each of these buildings is §HThe Creed of Servitude§! - a prayer of service to §HThe Grand Herald§! and its holy plan. The theory is that this is some kind of response to the doom foretold in §HThe Testament of Omen§!.

options.script:
name = DIG
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
地表勘探队伍有了一个有趣的发现。一段在某个主要城市中找到的视听记录。一大群生物，似乎就是当地的居民，正聚集在一个公共广场上。他们正在颂唱，合唱的声音不断增强，就像是有着旋律不断起伏的惊雷。

他们集体颂唱的歌词经翻译后为：“飞升已近。伟大先驱，携民如子，迈向新生。悲颓之地，弃之身后，应许家园，觅来繁星。吾辈追颂，如始如终！”
descriptions.en:
The surface expedition made an interesting find. It was a audio-visual recording from one of the major cities. A teeming mass of beings, seeming the bulk of the inhabitants, is crowding a public square. They are chanting, the collective voices rising in crescendo like the sound of a melodic, rolling thunderstorm.

The mass chant was translated as: "The ascension is nigh. Carry us, O Grand Herald, into a new beginning. Lead us from a land of tears and dust, and grant us a new home amongst the stars. We follow thee as one. We follow thee".

options.script:
name = DIG
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
§H追随者之颂唱§!不是一次孤立的事件——这起事件席卷全球，每个居民都在同时咏唱。在对这起不寻常的事件进行更深一步的调查后，我们对此事件有了更加清晰的了解。一份名为§H末日朝圣§!的文件已被发现，这似乎是与该神秘事件链真相有关的最后一环。

这份文件指出了这个行星上的一个特殊地点，一个用于开展最终清算或最终仪式的地方。那是一片在早先调查中被忽略的不起眼的沙漠。这份文件还提到了一个叫做§H揭纱秘仪§!的东西，目前正对其进行诠释。
descriptions.en:
§HThe Hymn of Following§! was not an isolated event - it was global, every single inhabitant chanting in unison. Such an unusual event warranted further research, and that's when a new insight was gained. A document called §HThe Pilgrimage of Last Days§! was uncovered, and it seems to be one of the last links in this mysterious chain of events.

The document refers to a specific location on the planet, where some final reckoning or ritual will occur; a swathe of unremarkable desert location neglected in earlier surveys. The document also speaks of something called §HThe Rite of Lifted Veil§!, which is now being interpreted.

options.script:
name = DIG
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
在轨道扫描中依靠精妙的光学伪装迷彩隐藏起来的§H伟大先知§!最终还是被发现了。它不是什么预言或者是宗教符号；它是一艘巨大的泰坦级宇宙飞船！以宗教名义发动的战争撕裂了他们的世界，这艘泰坦则被当作庇护一小部分人口的方舟，它将载着这些人离开这个临近末日的星球并前往一片未指明的应许之地。该舰船组装完成，运行正常，所以为什么它未能起飞实在是令人困惑。

看来在起飞前似乎发生了某种决战。一场极度残酷的战斗，没有任何一方在漫长的战斗后幸存。
descriptions.en:
Hidden from orbital scanning by sophisticated optical camouflage, §HThe Grand Herald§! was finally uncovered. It's not a prophet or religious figure; it is a gigantic Titan Class spaceship! Their world torn and dying due to wars carried out in the name of religion, the Titan was going to serve as an arkship for a fraction of the population, transporting them off the doomed planet and towards an unspecified promised land offworld. The ship is fully assembled and workable condition, so why it never took flight is puzzling.

It appears as if some final battle must have been fought just prior to takeoff. A struggle so fierce that neither side survived in the long run.

options.script:
name = SPLENDID
small_artifact_reward = yes
create_grand_herald = yes

descriptions.zh:
这根本就不是什么宗教事件！在关闭一处光学迷彩区域之后，考察队终于得以窥见§H伟大先驱§!的真实面貌；一艘巨大的泰坦级宇宙飞船，半截仍然埋在沙子之中，它被建造以对抗宇宙中即将到来的某种威胁。最终结果是，那些诗词般富含隐喻，被解释为宗教措辞的语言，其实只是这一物种平日里日常交谈的话语而已。

即将到来的危险是什么依旧是一个未解之谜，不过就目前所观察的来看，它一定在泰坦完全启动前已经来临。散布在舰船周围的是上千具已经灭绝的[FromFrom.Planet.GetName]的干尸，他们当时没能及时启动泰坦，以后也不会再有机会了。
descriptions.en:
It was never a religious archetype! After having deactivated an optical camouflage field, the expedition saw the true shape of §HThe Grand Herald§!; an immense Titan Class spaceship half-buried in the sand, built to fight some kind of approaching threat in space. As it turns out, the poetic, metaphorical nature of the native language - interpreted as being of religious expression - was in fact just the normal way this species communicated.

The nature of the oncoming menace is still a mystery, but from the looks of it, whatever it was seems to have arrived before the Titan was fully operational. Scattered around the ship are thousands of desiccated remains of the extinct species of [FromFrom.Planet.GetName]. They did not have time to activate their Titan, and they never will.

options.script:
name = SPLENDID
small_artifact_reward = yes
create_grand_herald = yes

descriptions.zh:
§H伟大先驱§!的确不是一个寻常的宗教符号，这是一个巨大而特别的工程项目——一个自动化的建造区域。其中高如摩天大楼的横梁揭示出其最初且唯一的项目；一艘巨大的泰坦级宇宙飞船。其宗教意义和目前考古成果的联系仍不完全明确，但我们已经知道了：§H圣约征兆§!中所说的危险最终到来，使得在伟大先驱工程完成之前，行星上的全部人口就已神秘死去。

但这个自动化的建造区域依旧不断工作，最终组装完成了这艘不会有乘客乘坐的飞船。这艘完整而空荡的飞船在无人驾驶的情况下静静地沉睡在此处，历经无数年华。我们要不要让它重见天日，驰骋于星海呢？
descriptions.en:
§HThe Grand Herald§! is an unconventional religious figure, indeed. It's a huge special engineering project - an automated construction yard. Its skyscraper-high spars still cradle its first and only product; a huge Titan Class spaceship. Where spiritual metaphor and archaeological fact intersect is still not entirely clear, but we know this: whatever threat §HThe Testament of Omen§! spoke of must have indeed come to pass, as the entire population died mysteriously prior to The Grand Herald project being concluded.

But the automated construction yard kept working, finalizing a ship without passengers. The mostly intact, empty ship has been slumbering here for eons without someone to pilot it. Shall we take it out for a spin?

name = SPLENDID

create_grand_herald = yes

descriptions.zh:
在[From.Planet.GetName]海域的探险遇到了一些奇怪的事情。大量有机物尖峰刺穿水面，向天空伸展数百米，其材质为珊瑚或动物骨骼。

尖峰以团簇的形式成打出现。这种构造在星球各处海域都很常见，除了最寒冷的极地海域。尖峰为多孔结构，其表面覆盖有大小不等的孔道，孔道尺寸与舰载机相当。也许这种生物结构与其繁殖过程有关？
descriptions.en:
The surface expedition down to the seas of [From.Planet.GetName] has come across something strange. Great spikes of organic material pierce the surface of the water, made from some kind of fossilized coral or bone, stretching hundreds of meters towards the sky.

The spikes are found in claw-like clusters of up to a few dozen, and formations like these are commonplace everywhere except the very coldest polar seas. The spikes are porous, covered with perforations ranging in size up to that of a strike craft. Perhaps they are related to how these bio-structures propagate themselves?

options.script:
name = DIG
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
探险队最终成功地在行星海底找到了一些长而均匀的生物构造。这些水下结构由与水面的尖峰材质相同，其运行机制类似于一种生物泵。该生物网络不断“呼吸”，呼吸搅动了海水。

这些构造的尺寸，以及其在海底的规模，暗示它们是造成[From.Planet.GetName]海面下难以解释的海水涌动的原因。
descriptions.en:
The expedition has finally managed to reach a set of long and evenly shaped bio-formations on the bottom of the planetary sea. Made of the same material as the surface-piercing spikes, these underwater formations appear to be some kind of organic pumping mechanism. The living network "breathes", and its exhalations cycle the current of the seas.

The size of these formations, as well as the sheer number of them across the ocean floor, hints that they are responsible for the unexplained underwater currents of [From.Planet.GetName].

options.script:
name = DIG
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
另一支深海探险队回来了，揭示了[FromFrom.Planet.GetName]海底暗流的真相。该星球上所有怪异的有机构造实际上都与一座巨大的珊瑚礁相连。事实证明，这种珊瑚在某种程度上是有意识的，尽管与我们这种感性生物相比，它有着完全不同的思维方式。通过在水中释放信息素，它或多或少地奴役了海洋中所有其他生物，控制它们的行为和繁殖周期，以满足自身的需要。

它似乎是完全无害的，但它仍然是一位木偶大师。它是这颗星球上最顶级的生命吗？或者是一只外来的寄生虫？与之沟通似乎是不可能的，所以我们可能永远不会知道真相了。
descriptions.en:
Another deep sea expedition has returned, and revealed the truth of the churning seas of [FromFrom.Planet.GetName]. All the strange organic formations on the planet are actually connected in a single, vast coral reef. This coral, as it turned out, is partly aware, although with an utterly alien mindset compared to our conception of sentient life. Through pheromones excreted in the water, it has more or less enslaved the rest of all the organisms in the sea, controlling their behavior and reproduction cycles to fit its own needs.

It seems to be completely benign, but it is a puppet master nonetheless. Is it simply the apex life form on this world? An intrusive alien parasite? Communicating with it seems impossible, so we may never know.

label.zh: 通过适应我们就不会遭受这样的入侵了。
label.en: In adapting, we will suffer no similar intrusions.

descriptions.zh:
在对这种外星生物的DNA进行测序后，我们得出了一个惊人的发现：遍布全球海洋的珊瑚网络不仅不是这个世界的原生物种，而且连自然物种都不是，它实际上是一个人造的生物工程产品。在厚厚的珊瑚层下面的是这世界整个生态系统灭绝生物的化石层。似乎珊瑚在被引入后，就逐渐扼杀了所有的本土生物，取而代之的是一个为自己量身定制的生态系统。

关于为什么要这样做，有两个主要的猜想：要么这种人造珊瑚是出于良性的原因被引入的，然后它以一种意想不到的方式在竞争中彻底击垮了原生物种；要么它是被故意设计成用来清除本地海洋世界的原生生物的可怕生物武器。
descriptions.en:
After sequencing the alien DNA, a startling revelation was made: the global sea coral network is not only not native to this world, but it is in fact a bio-engineered construct rather than a natural formation. Beneath the thick carpet of alien coral is a fossilized extinction layer of the entire previous ecosystem of this world. It seems the coral, once introduced, gradually choked out all the native life and replaced it with an ecosystem tailored specifically for itself.

There are two main theories as to why this might have been done: either the artificial coral was introduced for benign reasons, and then it massively out-competed the local wildlife in an unexpected way, or it was deliberately constructed to be some sort of terrifying biological weapon to cleanse ocean worlds of native life.

options.script: name = FASCINATING

label.zh: 通过适应我们就不会遭受这样的入侵了。
label.en: In adapting, we will suffer no similar intrusions.

descriptions.zh:
这是一台巨大的生物机器！地质分析表明，行星的海洋曾一度陷入死寂——没有洋流，也没有氧气来维持水生生物的生存。这种生物工程机器被引入该星球，目的是人为创造生物生存的基本先决条件。

显然它起作用了，因为现在在此星球上有着繁盛的水下动植物群。找不到任何线索来解释为何要进行如此巨大的工程，也没有找到由谁——或许是一种未知的水生物种，利用先进的生物技术进行环境改造，为自己创造一个新的家园？
descriptions.en:
It's all one giant bio-machine! Subsurface analysis indicates that the planet's oceans were once dead - no current or oxygen to sustain underwater life. This bio-engineered machine was introduced to the planet with the purpose of artificially jump starting the basic prerequisites of organic existence.

Apparently it worked, as underwater flora and fauna now thrives on the world. No trace was found of why such a colossal undertaking was carried out, nor by whom - was it perhaps some terraforming project by an unknown aquatic species with advanced biotechnology, seeking to create for themselves a new home?

options.script: name = UNFORTUNATE

label.zh: 通过适应我们就不会遭受这样的入侵了。
label.en: In adapting, we will suffer no similar intrusions.

descriptions.zh:
对[From.Planet.GetName]的仔细检查表明，广阔的海床看起来异常奇怪——像是卫星或小行星的表面，完全被撞击坑覆盖。这样的陨石坑一般不会出现在有大气层的天体上，特别是那些有海洋的天体上。

必须进行进一步的研究。
descriptions.en:
Closer inspection of [From.Planet.GetName] reveals that the bottom of the vast oceans look exceptionally strange - more like the surface of a moon or an asteroid - completely covered in impact craters. Craters like that tend to not appear on celestial bodies with atmosphere, and especially not on the ones with oceans.

Further studies must be made.

options.script:
name = DIG
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
海底神秘陨石坑的谜底终于在对水体的分析中找到了。某些矿物和化学成分的痕迹证明，这些水实际上并不来自同一颗行星。它以巨冰的形式被运到了这里，被扔到星球表面。冰块坠毁，破碎成碎片并融化，最终将整颗星球表面覆盖在水下。

这绝对是一项不朽的事业，但尚不清楚该工程究竟是为了什么目的而实施。
descriptions.en:
The answer to the mysterious craters in the ocean floor was finally found in an analysis of the water itself. Traces of certain minerals and chemical compositions proved that the water did in fact not belong to the same planet. It was transported here in the form of gargantuan blocks of ice that were hurled down on the planet. The ice blocks crashed, cracked into splinters and melted, eventually covering almost the entire surface with water.

It was an absolutely monumental undertaking, but there is nothing that hints to why it was carried out.

options.script:
name = DIG
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
[FromFrom.Planet.GetName]轨道上的科研船从海底深处检测到了一些不能识别的能量读数，仔细检查后，探险队发现了一座古代建筑。这是一个长达数公里的人工构造，只有一个功能：人为制造水下洋流。

水下循环对许多水生生物而言至关重要，目前的理论是，这颗行星由一些已能进行太空航行的水生物种改造成如今的模样。但好像他们从未露面。
descriptions.en:
The Science Ship in orbit of [FromFrom.Planet.GetName] picked up some unidentified energy readings from deep beneath the waves, and upon inspection the expedition discovered an ancient construction. A structure many kilometers long with a single purpose; to artificially create underwater currents.

Underwater circulation is vital for much aquatic life, and the current theory is that this planet was set up to be habitable for some aquatic, spacefaring species. It appears as if they never showed up.

descriptions.zh:
通过跟踪一个奇怪的能量信号，我们的探险队找到了一座埋在海底深处的外星通信阵列。若能翻译其包含的信息片段，便可得知外星引水工程的全貌。

根据翻译，整个造海项目是为了创造一座巨大的水下储仓，但它没有具体说明要存储什么东西。当然，该项目不需要淹没整颗星球。
descriptions.en:
By following a strange energy signature our expedition managed to locate an alien communications array buried deep in the seabed. It contained information fragments, and once translated they told of the water-introduction project.

According to the translation the entire ocean-making venture was done to create an immense submerged storage, but it does not specify what needed to be stored. Certainly not what requires an entire planet covered in water.

descriptions.zh:
多亏了科研船的意外发现，我们成功挖出了深埋在海底深处的古建筑。在那里进行探险活动非常困难，但结果是惊人的。

该建筑曾经是一个气候控制中心。它引导大型气候改造机器进入轨道。这是一个被中断的环境改造项目，但显然工程已经走得够远了。即使后续投入中断了，但有蓬勃的自然演化接手后续工作，最终创造了现在的生态系统。
descriptions.en:
Thanks to serendipitous sensory scan the Science Ship managed to isolate ancient building buried deep under the ocean floor. Getting the expedition there turned out to be very difficult, but the finding was grand.

The building was once a climate control center. It directed giant climate-altering machines in orbit. This was a terraforming project that was interrupted, but apparently the project had gotten far enough. Even without directed input, nature managed to thrive and eventually create the ecosystem that can be seen today.

descriptions.zh: 登陆到[From.Planet.GetName]表面的探险队开始调查其中一个圆形岛屿，并很快有了不同寻常的发现。岛下有一套复杂的隧道网络，蜿蜒穿过奇特的油性岩层。这些隧道呈均匀的圆形，并且在所有岛屿下面都能发现。它们似乎是自然形成而非人工挖掘出的，但它们的形成方式肯定与通常的地质运动不同。
descriptions.en: The surface expedition sent down to [From.Planet.GetName] started to investigate one of the round islands, and soon made a remarkable discovery. The island had a complex tunnel network running beneath it, winding through the strange, oily rock. These tunnels were remarkably even and round, and laced the entire island. They seem to be natural formations, not intentionally excavated, but they have certainly not been shaped in a conventional, geological manner.

options.script:
name = DIG
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh: 地面探险队深入圆形岛屿时，又有两项新的发现：第一，每个岛的下面似乎都有重复的内部隧道布局。它们的大小略有不同，但布局是一样的。第二个发现更令人惊讶：这些岛屿不是地壳的一部分——它们实际上是漂浮的！它们的下层充满了气囊，它们与相当脆弱和多孔的岛屿岩石相结合，让这些岛漂了起来。
descriptions.en: As the surface expedition delved deeper into the round islands, two more discoveries were made: First, that every island seem to have a duplicate internal layout of tunnels beneath them. They vary slightly in size, but not in how they are laid out. The second discovery was even more astonishing: the islands aren't parts of the planet crust - they actually float! Their lower levels are filled with pockets of gas, which combined with the fairly brittle and porous island rock makes then buoyant.

options.script:
name = DIG
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh: 关于浮岛之谜的答案不是在地质学领域找到的，而是在生物学领域。这些岛屿实际上是巨大的水母化石。数百万年前的冰河时代把它们都冻死了，之后它们的尸体变成了化石，形成了今天看到的漂浮在水面上的岛屿。长年累月的碎屑堆积使它们裸露的表面看起来像天然岛屿，但它们的下面完全是有机的。
descriptions.en: The answer to the mystery of the floating islands was not found in the field of geology, but in biology. The islands are in fact enormous fossilized jellyfish creatures. Millions of years ago an ice age froze them all to death, after which their carcasses were fossilized into the islands seen bobbing around in the water today. Ages of debris accretion gave their exposed surface the look of natural islands, but beneath that they are entirely organic.

label.en: A tasty looking patch of ground.

descriptions.zh: 它们根本不是岛屿，而是水母！事实上，每一个漂浮的圆圈都是一头巨大的无脊椎动物。而且他们没有死去：看似石化的状态只是他们生命周期中的一个自然组成部分。在数千年的时间里，这些石质岛屿释放出沉积物，直到它们完全溶解。沉积物中含有微小的水螅虫，这些水螅虫最终会在水中出芽，直到它们进入生命周期的下一阶段。
descriptions.en: They are not islands at all, but jellyfish! Each of these floating circles is in fact a giant invertebrate organism. And they aren't dead, either: the seemingly fossilized state is just a natural part of their life cycle. Over the course of thousands of years, these stony islands release sediment until they finally dissolve completely. The sediment contains microscopic polyps that eventually germinate in the water until they enter the next stage of their life cycle.

descriptions.zh: 它们根本不是岛屿。它们全是外星生物：水母生物，它们出于某些原因被人工地引入了生态系统。然而，它们的引入似乎并没有严格按计划进行。大部分大型的水母生物死去并变成了化石，再演变成浮岛群，但是较小的水母生物适应了环境，它们现在在行星上的海洋中繁衍生息。它们最终是否会步更大体型祖先的后尘还需拭目以待。
descriptions.en: They aren't islands at all. They are all alien organisms: jellyfish creatures that for some reason were artificially introduced to the ecosystem. It seems their introduction did not go exactly as planned, however. Most of the big ones died and fossilized - becoming the floating island archipelago - but the smaller jellyfish creatures assimilated and are now thriving in the oceans across the planet. Whether they will eventually share the fate of their bigger ancestors remains to be seen.

label.en: A tasty looking patch of ground.

descriptions.zh:
通过追踪很可能是太空舰船留下的微弱的能量痕迹，一颗特殊的小行星从星团中被挑选了出来。对小行星表面的进行了更仔细的调察后，在岩石表面发现了多处着陆和起飞的迹象，这证实了此处先前存在太空航线的理论。

传感器还显示出小行星内部有被挖空的区域和隧道，可以用来发掘更多的信息。
descriptions.en:
By tracing weak energy trails - most likely left by space-faring vessels - one particular asteroid in the cluster was singled out. Closer inspection of the asteroid's surface confirmed the theory of prior space traffic as multiple signs of landing and takeoff were found on the rocky exterior.

Sensors also indicate cavities and tunnels within the asteroid, which may be excavated.

options.script:
name = DIG
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
在穿过狭小的隧道之后，探险队终于跌跌撞撞地进入了最深处的密室，这是一个巨大而做工精致的房间，里面装饰着直接雕刻在岩石上的雕塑。刻在墙上的宗教文本把这里叫做成“第九步”，显然这里是创建该处的物种进行宗教之旅的众多目的地之一。

如果这是第九步，那前八步在哪里？接下来还有几步？
descriptions.en:
Following small and narrow tunnels, the expedition team finally stumbled into the innermost sanctum; a vast and exquisitely crafted chamber adorned by sculptures carved directly into the rock. Translation of spiritual texts carved into the walls called the place "The Ninth Step", and it was apparently one of many destinations on a religious journey taken by the creating species.

If this was the ninth step, where are the preceding eight? And how many steps followed?

descriptions.zh:
当表面探险队发现了大量的储存区和挖入小行星的地窖后，这颗小行星被频繁造访的原因就变得显而易见了。这块废石曾是某种能够进行太空航行的物种的仓库，在将船只送入更深远的太空之前提供燃料补给和维护。这意味着那是一个没有超光速引擎的外星社会，但其拥有探索太空的充足动力。

小行星仓库被废弃的原因尚未明确，但我们设法回收了少量的物资。谁找到的就是谁的！
descriptions.en:
The reasons behind this well-visited asteroid became clear as the surface expedition encountered vast storage areas and silos dug into the asteroid. The dead rock served as a depot for some space-faring species, offering refueling and maintenance before sending ships even deeper into space. This would indicate an alien society devoid of FTL drive, but with an abundance of motivation to explore space.

Why the asteroid depot was abandoned remains unclear, but we managed to salvage a small yield of materials. Finders keepers!

descriptions.zh:
进入小行星内部后，探险队有了一个相当吸引人的发现。废弃的冷冻舱——成千上万个——排列在巨大的人工挖掘出的空间里。每一个冷冻舱都打开着，早已停止了运转，让人感觉它们已经完成了使命。

目前的理论是，这颗小行星就像是某种殖民飞船，被投射出去，穿越茫茫太空，飞向某个繁荣的栖息地。当接近目的地时，自动系统唤醒了沉睡的“货物”，然后他们搭乘短途宇宙飞船离开了小行星，前往他们的新家。
descriptions.en:
Getting inside the asteroid, the expedition made quite a fascinating discovery. Abandoned cryo-pods - hundreds of thousands of them - lined vast, dug out chambers. Each pod was opened and inactive, giving the impression that they had already fulfilled their purpose.

The current theory is that the asteroid served as some kind of colonization shuttle, hurled through space toward some prosperous habitat. When in proximity to its destination, automated systems woke up the slumbering cargo, and they left the asteroid in short-distance spacecraft to get to their new home.

descriptions.zh:
与在[From.Planet.GetName]表面上遇到的复杂情况相比，在轨科研船的传感器引发的骚动简直是小巫见大巫。来源不明的极端磁场波动甚至使设备失控。

研究这种电磁混乱将是一个相当严峻的考验——但只要有足够的时间，我们会得到答案的。
descriptions.en:
The disturbances caused by the orbiting Science Ship's sensors are nothing compared to the complications being encountered down on the surface of [From.Planet.GetName]. Extreme magnetic fluctuations from some unknown source are making equipment go haywire.

It will be quite an ordeal to research this electromagnetic bedlam - but given enough time, answers will emerge.

options.script:
name = DIG
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
就在地面考察队设法排除了失灵设备的故障后，剧烈波动的天然磁场终于揭开了它的神秘面纱。

[From.Planet.GetName]上汹涌的熔岩海洋与岩浆河流并非是普通的岩浆——那是熔融的金属！这种温度下的金属不会呈现出太强的磁性，[From.Planet.GetName]上的熔融金属更是不可能产生如此规模的电磁场。这究竟是怎么一回事？
descriptions.en:
Once the surface expedition managed to solve the problems with the malfunctioning equipment, the nature of the wild magnetic fluctuations started to reveal itself.

The raging oceans and rivers of lava down on [From.Planet.GetName] are in fact not made up of conventional magma - it's molten metal! Metals of this temperature tend not to have particularly strong magnetic properties; not even the sheer volume of molten metal on [From.Planet.GetName] should create electromagnetism on this scale. So what is causing it?

options.script:
name = DIG
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
[FromFrom.Planet.GetName]轨道上的这艘科学飞船终于解开了行星磁场波动之谜。

数百万年前，这颗行星靠近了一种特殊的中子星。这颗中子星的磁性或多或少地把[FromFrom.Planet.GetName]内部的金属熔化了。将它们变成我们今天看到的熔融海洋。目前所遇到的电磁现象，与诱发的大灾变的电磁现象相比，绝对是小巫见大巫。

那颗中子星现在在哪里仍然是个谜。一个相当令人不安的谜。
descriptions.en:
The Science Ship orbiting [FromFrom.Planet.GetName] has finally cracked the enigma of the magnetic fluctuations down on the planet.

Millions of years ago, the planet came into close proximity with a special kind of neutron star. The magnetism of this neutron star effectively boiled the metals inside [FromFrom.Planet.GetName], turning them into the molten oceans we see today. The electromagnetism we've encountered is but a lingering echo of the original, cataclysmic event.

Where the neutron star is now remains a mystery - a quite disturbing mystery.

descriptions.zh:
对传统物理定律的公然漠视使得科学部门认为“外力”可以解释[FromFrom.Planet.GetName]的奇怪特性。

撞击坑——以及轨道上的核聚变驱动粒子痕迹——表明这颗行星实际上在某个时刻被某种超级电子武器击中。这次严重的冲击使得行星上所有的金属都熔化了，而行星上仍然充斥着“残余电荷”。

究竟是什么导致了如此可怕的攻击，我们不得而知。
descriptions.en:
The blatant disregard for conventional laws of physics has our science department considering "external forces" as an explanation for the strange properties of [FromFrom.Planet.GetName].

An impact crater - in combination with fusion drive particle traces found in orbit - suggests that the planet was fired upon by some kind of electric super-weapon at some point. The severity of the strike was such that all metals on the planet melted, and the planet is still crackling with residual electricity.

What warranted such tremendous attack? We'll never know.

descriptions.zh:
传感器重新校准后，抵消了干扰的它立马有了新发现：一个邻近卫星上的废弃研究站。几近彻底烧毁的记录中抢救出的数据碎片详细描述了一个涉及星球表面巨型人造磁铁的实验。

实验有些过于成功了。它将整个行星的金属外壳变成了熔池，无比强烈的电磁电荷瞬间就炸毁了研究站。

嗯……没有牺牲就没有进展。
descriptions.en:
Once the sensors had been re-calibrated to compensate for the interference, a new discovery was made: an abandoned research station, located on a nearby moon. Fragments of data were salvaged from the almost entirely burned-out records, detailing an experiment involving a giant, artificial magnet on the planet's surface.

The experiment was a bit too successful. It turned the planet's entire, metal crust into molten pools with an electromagnetic charge so intense that it fried the research station in an instant.

Well... No progress without sacrifice.

descriptions.zh: 对文物的研究一定程度上促进了我们的部分科研。
descriptions.en: Study of the artifacts has advanced some of our research.

descriptions.zh: 虽然我们正在研究的文物没有给予我们研究上立竿见影的突破，但它们正在加速我们所有领域的科研。
descriptions.en: While the artifacts we are researching have not yielded an immediate breakthrough, they are accelerating research in all fields.

descriptions.zh: 对文物的研究让我们的研究取得了意料之外的突破！
descriptions.en: Study of the artifacts has yielded an unexpected breakthrough!

descriptions.zh: 我们应该把重点放在哪儿？
descriptions.en: What aspect shall we focus on?

tooltips.zh: 你的士兵现在更强壮，更具有攻击性，更令人畏惧，但警惕性却有所下降。
tooltips.en: Your soldiers are stronger, more aggressive, and terrifying, but a bit less careful.

tooltips.zh: 舰队安全阈值的调整以潜在地损失些许命中率为代价来提高伤害。
tooltips.en: Adjustments to the safety thresholds of your armies increases their damage potential at the cost of a minor loss in accuracy.

tooltips.zh: 你的舰船武器被调整为对护盾造成额外伤害。
tooltips.en: Your ship weapons are tuned to deal additional damage to shields.

tooltips.zh: 你的舰船能通过利用敌舰的缺陷来对其装甲造成额外伤害。
tooltips.en: Your ship weapons are able to exploit weaknesses, dealing additional damage to armor.

descriptions.zh: 我们应该把重点放在哪儿？
descriptions.en: What aspect shall we focus on?

tooltips.zh: 对稀有文物的研究意外地在帝国境内快速掀起了一股潮流。每个帝国公民都参与其中。
tooltips.en: The study of minor artifacts has unexpectedly launched a viral fad across your Empire. Everybody's doing it.

tooltips.zh: 对稀有文物的研究让我们的生产效率得到了有效提高。
tooltips.en: Study of minor artifacts have yielded efficiency boosts to general manufacturing.

tooltips.zh: 对稀有文物的研究，让我们的个人电子元件的电池尺寸减少了3%，它们现在变得比以前更加轻薄，并且生产成本更低。
tooltips.en: Study of minor artifacts have yielded a 3% reduction in the battery size of personal electronics, allowing them to become thinner and cheaper to build than ever before!

tooltips.zh: 我们对稀有文物的研究所揭示的技巧已被我们的维护子个体所采用。
tooltips.en: Our study of minor artifacts has uncovered techniques for our maintenance drones to exploit.

tooltips.zh: 对稀有文物的研究，让我们的小型电子元件的电池尺寸减少了3%，提高了我们的效率。
tooltips.en: Study of minor artifacts has yielded a 3% reduction in the battery size of small electronics, increasing our efficiency.

tooltips.zh: 对古老知识的学习以及团队建设活动使您的领袖更加富有洞察力。
tooltips.en: Ancient lessons and team building exercises have provided new insights to your leaders.

tooltips.zh: 对稀有遗物的研究让我们能够强化我们自身的信息素，这使得领袖的工作变得更加容易。
tooltips.en: Study of minor artifacts has allowed us to enhance our pheromones, making it easier to lead.

tooltips.zh: 通过研究稀有文物，让我们为领袖设计了稍微更高效的算法。
tooltips.en: Study of minor artifacts has yielded slightly more efficient algorithms for our leaders.

descriptions.zh:
[From.Owner.GetName]至伟至耀，巨型艺术设施上鳞次栉比的展位均被无价的文物填满。

异种将仰望我们的造业，甚惶甚恐。
descriptions.en:
The greatness of the [From.Owner.GetName] is such that we can line the Exhibition Stations of our Mega Art Installation with priceless artifacts.

Let the xenos look upon our works and despair.

descriptions.zh:
无价的文物填满了展览站，带给我们对过往的一瞥，赋予我们对未来的灵感。

今天可谓荣耀。
descriptions.en:
Priceless artifacts fill the Exhibition Stations, bringing the past to the present to inspire the future.

This is a glorious day.

options.script: name = EXCELLENT

descriptions.zh: 尽管生物学领域的积累并未救伊拉斯人于水火，但是他们，毫无疑问，是这一方面的专家。我们的科学家已从他们的发现中吸取了富有价值的经验。
descriptions.en: Though it clearly did not save them, the Irassians were admittedly experts in the field of biology. Our scientists have adapted what was worthwhile from their findings.

descriptions.zh: 我们已成功将伊拉斯人的文物融入我们的科研进程。他们对生命科学的见解将极大地帮助我们。
descriptions.en: We have successfully managed to integrate the Irassian artifacts into our research process. Their insights into biological research will greatly aid our own.

descriptions.zh: 我们的科学家开始了一个新的特殊项目，以探索先驱者更深处的秘密。
descriptions.en: Our scientists have begun a special project to study the deeper secrets of the precursors.

options.script: name = progress.2.a.mech

descriptions.zh:
尤特有一套可以高效清除其孵化场星球上敌对异种生物的工序。我们已经成功恢复了这一净化工序。

这确实会对生物圈造成或多或少惹人非议的短期影响，但一旦其恢复完好，这颗行星应该会更符合我们的需求。
descriptions.en:
The Yuht had efficient processes for removing hostile xeno presences from their hatchery worlds. We have successfully recreated this cleansing process.

It does have some concerning short term effects on the biosphere, but once it recovers, the planet should be more suitable to our needs.

descriptions.zh:
我们已经设法重现了尤特过去用于预处理其孵化场星球的净化工序。

这确实会对生物圈造成或多或少惹人非议的短期影响，但一旦其恢复完好，这颗行星应该会更符合我们的需求。
descriptions.en:
We have managed to recreate the cleansing process that the Yuht would use to prepare their hatchery worlds.

It does have some concerning short term effects on the biosphere, but once it recovers, the planet should be more suitable to our needs.

tooltips.en: Colony Decision Unlocked: §YInitiate Yuht Cleansing Process§!

tooltips.zh: 解锁殖民地决议：§Y启动尤特净化工序§!
tooltips.en: Colony Decision Unlocked: §YInitiate Yuht Cleansing Process§!

descriptions.zh: 第一联盟证明了信赖其他种族是愚蠢的，这只会招致孱弱不堪和自我毁灭。然而，他们的一些先进建筑方法，或许多少能够为我们所用。
descriptions.en: The First League proves that reliance on other races is folly that leads to weakness and self-destruction. Some of their advanced construction methods may, however, be of possible use.

descriptions.zh: 我们已成功将第一联盟文物融入我们的科研进程。他们对工业科技的见解将极大地帮助我们。
descriptions.en: We have successfully managed to integrate the First League artifacts into our research process. Their insights into industrial research will greatly aid our own.

descriptions.zh: 赛博勒克斯的传说证明了我们取缔人工智能的决策是无比明智的。好在他们的某些与巨型结构工程相关的发现可能对我们的事业有所裨益。
descriptions.en: The tale of the Cybrex is proof that our decision to outlaw artificial intelligence is a wise one.  Some of their findings related to megastructure engineering have the potential to be beneficial to our cause.

descriptions.zh: 我们已成功将赛博勒克斯文物融入我们的科研进程。他们对巨型结构工程的见解将极大地帮助我们。
descriptions.en: We have successfully managed to integrate the Cybrex artifacts into our research process. Their insights into megastructure engineering will greatly aid our own.

descriptions.zh: 沃陶姆看上去在研究过程中采纳了一些不合逻辑的概念。他们在计算机以及虚拟世界领域的一些先进之处应该整合进我们的研究进程中。
descriptions.en: The Vultaum appear to have accepted some fundamentally illogical concepts in their research. Their research into computing and virtual worlds had some advances that we shall incorporate into our own processes.

descriptions.zh: 沃陶姆痴迷于现实和虚拟世界的概念。他们大多数发现对我们来说都毫无意义，但是至少他们对计算机的研究能够帮助我们。
descriptions.en: The Vultaum obsessed over the concept of reality and of virtual worlds. Most of their findings are useless to us, but at least their research into computing will aid our own.

descriptions.zh:
沃陶姆在计算机和虚拟世界领域是无可置疑的大师。我们可以使用他们的发现来极大帮助我们在该领域的研究。

然而，他们的结论却引发了我们的忧虑。乍一看来这些结论不仅缺陷重重还毫无意义，但是随着研究的深入，我们认为他们似乎发现了真相的冰山一角。

如果还想要进一步探究，我们将需要更多的时间和资源。
descriptions.en:
The Vultaum were undisputed masters at computing and virtual worlds. We will be able to use their findings to dramatically aid our own research into these fields.

Their conclusions are troubling, however. At first glance they appear to be fundamentally flawed nonsense, but upon deeper inspection they seem to have elements of truth to them.

If we wish to delve deeper, we will require additional time and resources.

descriptions.zh: 尽管在结论上存在着根本性缺陷，沃陶姆在计算机及虚拟世界领域极其先进，能够极大的帮助我们的相关研究。
descriptions.en: Despite the fundamentally flawed conclusions, the Vultaum research into computing and virtual worlds was highly advanced and will dramatically aid our own studies.

tooltips.en: We have gained [crisobj_thesis_value] £advanced_logic£ §YAdvanced Logic§!.

tooltips.zh: 我们获得了[crisobj_thesis_value]£advanced_logic£§Y超然逻辑§!。
tooltips.en: We have gained [crisobj_thesis_value] £advanced_logic£ §YAdvanced Logic§!.

tooltips.zh: 我们获得了[crisobj_thesis_value]£advanced_logic£§Y超然逻辑§!。
tooltips.en: We have gained [crisobj_thesis_value] £advanced_logic£ §YAdvanced Logic§!.

label.zh: 我们会好好利用已学到的知识。
label.en: We will put what we have already learned to good use.

tooltips.zh: 我们获得了[crisobj_thesis_value]£advanced_logic£§Y超然逻辑§!。
tooltips.en: We have gained [crisobj_thesis_value] £advanced_logic£ §YAdvanced Logic§!.

label.zh: 继续深挖，我们一定要学到他们知道的一切。
label.en: Dig deeper. We must know everything they learned.

tooltips.zh: 我们获得了[crisobj_thesis_value]£advanced_logic£§Y超然逻辑§!。
tooltips.en: We have gained [crisobj_thesis_value] £advanced_logic£ §YAdvanced Logic§!.

descriptions.zh:
看起来，沃陶姆竟然有可能是对的。

我们重复了他们的实验，然后得到了相近的结论。我们有一定可能真的存在于一个虚拟世界中。

我们缺乏足够的信息，无法得知是谁因为什么理由才会创造这样一个世界。但可以肯定的是，没有人会残酷到仅仅因为好玩就创造一个宇宙。

这件事情的影响是深远的，我们现在恭敬的请求您下一步的指示。
descriptions.en:
It seems that the Vultaum may have been correct after all.

We have replicated their experiments and come to similar conclusions. There is a moderate chance that we are, in fact, existing within a simulated world.

We do not have enough data to hypothesize why someone would create such a thing. Surely no one would create a universe as cruel and cold as this one for simple enjoyment.

The implications of this are profound, and we yield to your discretion as to our next steps.

label.zh: 令人不安，封锁这个调查的相关信息。

tooltips.zh: 我们获得了[crisobj_thesis_value]£advanced_logic£§Y超然逻辑§!。
tooltips.en: We have gained [crisobj_thesis_value] £advanced_logic£ §YAdvanced Logic§!.

label.en: The people have the right to know.

tooltips.zh: 我们获得了[crisobj_thesis_value]£advanced_logic£§Y超然逻辑§!。
tooltips.en: We have gained [crisobj_thesis_value] £advanced_logic£ §YAdvanced Logic§!.

公众因得知真相而感到§R困扰§!。

tooltips.en:
The public are §Rdisturbed§! by the revelation.

descriptions.zh:
我们遗憾的通知您，领导沃陶姆研究项目的科学家[leading_vultaum_research_scientist.GetName]并未决定停止研究沃陶姆。

他们留下的笔记开始变得逻辑混乱，直至成为胡言乱语。他们随之决定要“继续研究”，此后不久便自杀了。
descriptions.en:
We regret to inform you that [leading_vultaum_research_scientist.GetName] did not take the decision to end the research into the Vultaum well.

The notes they left behind drift off into mad ramblings before coming to the decision to 'continue the research', shortly before committing suicide.

descriptions.zh:
报告表明，[leading_vultaum_research_scientist.GetName]已经饱受领导沃陶姆研究的压力影响。

他们开始能够进行难以置信的逻辑跳跃，使得我们的研究大大受益，但是同时他们也不得不自行用药治疗，以作为高压下的应对机制。
descriptions.en:
Reports indicate that the stress of leading the research into the Vultaum has affected [leading_vultaum_research_scientist.GetName].

They have begun to make incredible leaps of logic that are greatly aiding our research, but have also begun self-medicating as a coping mechanism.

descriptions.zh: 报告称，[leading_vultaum_research_scientist.GetName]已经开始能够进行难以想象的逻辑跳跃，这使我们的研究项目受益匪浅。
descriptions.en: Reports indicate that [leading_vultaum_research_scientist.GetName] has benefited greatly the research project, and has begun to make incredible leaps of logic that are greatly aiding our research.

descriptions.zh:
通过研究巴奥的资料，我们对行星生命播种及环境改造过程都有了新的认识。

在仔细研究巴奥失去感知能力的变化过程后，我们也了解了诸多关于提升技术的知识，但我们已经掌握这项技术了。
descriptions.en:
Studying the Baol has given us new insights into the spread of plant life and improved our terraforming processes.

By carefully tracking the changes that the Baol underwent during their loss of sentience we also learned much about the uplifting process, but have already mastered that technology.

descriptions.zh:
在仔细研究巴奥失去感知能力的变化过程后，我们已经获得了足够的知识以逆转此过程。

我们也同样对行星生命播种及环境改造技术有了新的认识。
descriptions.en:
By carefully tracking the changes that the Baol underwent during their loss of sentience, we have gained much knowledge on how to reverse that process.

We have also gained new insights into the spread of plant life and improved our terraforming processes.

descriptions.zh: 我们已成功将泽珞族文物融入我们的科研进程。他们对灵能研究的洞见将极大地帮助我们。
descriptions.en: We have successfully managed to integrate the Zroni artifacts into our research process. Their insights into psionic study will greatly aid our own research.

descriptions.zh:
这座废墟看起来至少有成百上千年那么陈旧了。起初它看起来只是一个大型露天建筑，不过随着对外部结构发掘的深入，我们很快发现这只是一座城市中被废弃的贫民窟。有一座巨大的大门阻挡了我们深入城市的去路，我们的科学家猜想这个社会分为了数个阶层，而建筑的每一层分别居住着这座城市一个阶层的人。

我们的科学家很快就在这座地下废墟破碎的混凝土地面下发现了外星人的遗骸。然而在找到第一具遗骸过后，我们很快发现贫民窟里到处都是遗骸，有的横尸街头，有的死在家中，有的从天花板上高高地悬挂下来。虽然不知道是谁干的，但真的是一副相当令人反胃的场景。
descriptions.en:
The ruins seem to be centuries, if not millennia, old. At first it seems to be only a large open-air dome, but as we are excavating the outermost parts we quickly find ourselves in what appears to be the derelict slums of a city. As a large gate blocks our progress deeper into the city, our scientists speculate that it is split into a hierarchy, each layer holding one class of the people of the city.

It does not take long before one of our scientists finds alien remains in subterranean ruins under the broken concrete floor. After the first corpse is found, however, we start finding remains all over the slums, be it in the streets, in what would have been their homes, or hanging from the most remote parts of the ceiling. It is unclear what killed them, but it is a grisly sight.

label.zh: 那么其他层里又为我们隐藏着什么呢？
label.en: What do the other layers have in store for us?

options.script:
name = ancrel.11000.a
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
第一个圈子似乎是由流浪汉和贫民们摇摇欲坠的窝棚组成，而第二个圈子则与[Root.GetAdj]市政规划观念有很多一致之处。

我们发现了几个我们的科学家认为曾经是集市的开放广场，但因为年深日久，所有东西都早已腐朽到无法辨认它可能是什么的地步。

之后不久，我们也开始在圆顶的这一部分发现值得注意的遗迹。此处居民尸骸遍地，其死亡方式似乎与他们那些穷邻居差不多。
descriptions.en:
Whereas the first circle seemingly consisted of the ramshackle dwellings of the outcast and destitute, this second circle has more in common with the [Root.GetAdj] notion of proper urban planning.

We find several open squares our scientists assume used to be marketplaces, though anything from back then has long since decayed to the point where it is impossible to make out what it might have been.

It does not take long before we start finding unusual remains in this part of the dome too. They seem to have perished in much the same way as their poorer neighbors, and we find the dead strewn all over.

options.script:
name = ancrel.11005.a
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
当进入第三层的大门最终打开后，我们的科学家们——带着对下一步的发现的好奇——鱼贯而入，而这里很快被确认为是该穹顶古建筑中的一个更富有的区域。我们可就此对从这座城市可能获得的发现做出更积极的期望。

进入这一层后不久，我们中的一个人突然转身，野蛮地袭击了一位同事。当该袭击者被制服时，受害者已经死在地上。此后，那位发疯的科学家一直胡言乱语，我们完全无法理解他们身上到底发生了什么。

这一层比前两层都小，很可能是我们到达圆顶中心之前的最后一层。只剩下一扇门了。
descriptions.en:
When the gate into the third layer finally opens, our scientists - curious about what they will find next - flood into what is soon identified as a yet wealthier region of the old dome. At this point we can make confident assumptions about what to expect from this city.

Shortly after we enter the layer, one of our people suddenly turns around and savagely attacks a colleague. The victim is already dead on the ground by the time the unexpected assailant is restrained. In the aftermath we are completely unable to get anything sensible out of the crazed scientist, and get no better understanding of what happened to them.

This layer is significantly smaller than either of the previous two, and it is most likely the final one before we reach the center of the dome. Only one gate remains.

label.zh: 我们的科学家随时准备探索最后一层。
label.en: Our scientists stand ready to check the final layer.

options.script:
name = ancrel.11010.a
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
当最后一扇门开启时，强烈的灵能波冲击着我们的科学家。他们中的大多数在剧烈的痛苦中崩溃了，最终只有少数人进入了这一层。

这一层似乎是一座大寺庙，中间有一个巨大的祭台或祭坛。墙上到处都是描绘不同恒星系的巨大图表，一个重复的图表似乎围绕着[Root.System.GetName]本身。

幸存为数不多的的几位科学家向中央靠拢，他们发现这实际上是一台打造成古老祭坛形式的雄伟机器。
descriptions.en:
As soon as the final gate opens up, waves of intense psionic energy wash upon our scientists. Most of them collapse in apparent agony, leaving only a few to make their way into the actual layer itself.

It seems to be a large temple, with a massive dais or altar in the middle of it. All across the walls there are huge diagrams of different star systems, and a repeated one seems to center on [Root.System.GetName] itself.

Making their way closer to the middle, the few scientists that remain find that it is in fact an imposing machine fashioned in the form of an old altar.

label.zh: 让我们修一下这台机器，看看能发现什么。
label.en: Let us tinker with this machine and see what we can find.

descriptions.zh: 当修理工作开始时，他们突然被一种共同的幻觉所困扰——一个正被挖出并解封的存在，尖啸着发出命令。尖啸越发刺耳，一个生物撕开[From.System.GetName]星系的景象在他们的脑海中反复上演。几位科学家不省人事，无法应对这种持续折磨他们身体疼痛。
descriptions.en: As they start tinkering with the machine, they are suddenly beset by a shared auditory hallucination - a screaming command by something to be unearthed, unshackled. Visions of a creature ripping apart the [From.System.GetName] system plays repeatedly in their heads as the creature's demands grow shriller. Several scientists fall unconscious, unable to deal with the unabating torrents of pain that rack their bodies.

label.zh: 拆了这台机器，以免造成更多的伤害！
label.en: Rip the machine apart before it can cause any more harm!

tooltips.zh: 一个§Y诡异之魇§!将被释放到§Y[eldritch_location.GetName]§!恒星系中。
tooltips.en: An §YEldritch Horror§! will be released in the §Y[eldritch_location.GetName]§! system.

descriptions.zh:
终于……

凡人，跪下！在我面前卑躬屈膝，我将赐予你佑护和智慧。

若敢不从，我将为你带来终结！
descriptions.en:
FINALLY...

BOW DOWN MORTALS, GROVEL BEFORE ME, AND I SHALL GRANT YOU PROTECTION AND WISDOM.

OPPOSE ME, AND I SHALL BE YOUR END!

label.zh: 啊，伟大的存在！来拥抱你迷途的羊群吧！
label.en: O Great One! Embrace your wayward flock!

tooltips.zh: §Y[Root.GetName]§!将重建在§Y[eldritch_location.GetName]§!的恒星基地
tooltips.en: §Y[Root.GetName]§! will rebuild their starbase in the §Y[eldritch_location.GetName]§! system.

label.en: It was a mistake to release you.

tooltips.zh: §Y[Root.GetName]§!将会与§Y诡异之魇§!进入敌对。
tooltips.en: §Y[Root.GetName]§! will become hostile to the §YEldritch Horror§!.

descriptions.zh:
尔等既选择了智慧之路。
一切将如其之所应为。
descriptions.en:
SO YOU HAVE CHOSEN THE PATH OF WISDOM.
EVERYTHING IS AS IT SHOULD BE.

label.zh: 一切将如您所愿，伟大的存在。
label.en: It will be as you wish, Great One.

options.script: name = ancrel.11027.a

descriptions.zh: 尔等既选择了死亡。
descriptions.en: SO YOU HAVE CHOSEN DEATH.

options.script: name = ancrel.11030.a

descriptions.zh: 我们与我们穿越[eldritch_location.GetName]星系的舰队失去了联系。随后，我们又收到了其中恒星坍缩和一切毁灭的消息。
descriptions.en: We have lost all contact with our fleet as it was traveling through the [eldritch_location.GetName] system. Shortly afterwards, we receive news about the collapse of the star and the destruction of everything around it.

options.script: name = ancrel.11035.a

descriptions.zh: [Root.Leader.GetName]与一组研究人员登上了空间站，并设法恢复了某些部分的供电。似乎在 [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural]进入太空之前仅仅几个世纪就已经有人居住了。乍一看，它似乎是一个武装空间站，占其大部分体积的超大大炮证明了这一点。然而，其余大部分区域似乎都专门设计为研究设施，这表明该武器很可能是高度实验性的。
descriptions.en: [Root.Leader.GetName] has boarded the station with a team of researchers and managed to restore power to some sections. It appears that it was inhabited mere centuries before [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural] took to space. At first sight, it appears to have been a weapons station, as evidenced by the exceptionally large cannon that takes up the majority of its volume. However, most of the remaining sections seem to have been dedicated to research facilities, indicating that the weapon was likely highly experimental.

options.script:
name = INTERESTING
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
[Root.Leader.GetName]不禁注意到，即便考虑到空间站的年龄，其明显未损坏的系统绝大部分似乎以过高的频率出现故障。

在无数次重新激活它们后，团队的计算技术人员发出痛苦的尖叫：“这是啥？为啥？咋整？！”一时间，痛苦和怀疑的声音有增无减，[Root.Leader.GetSheHe]摇了摇[Root.Leader.GetHerHis]的头，宣布失败。“似乎整个设施都是用导管胶带糊在一起的，”[Root.Leader.GetSheHe]说。“我很震惊这玩意儿曾经能用。”
descriptions.en:
[Root.Leader.GetName] can't help but notice that an abnormally large number of apparently undamaged systems in the station seem to be failing with excessive frequency, even allowing for their age.

Upon reactivating them for the umpteenth time, agonized screams are heard from the team's comp tech: "What? Why? How?!" The stream of distressed and incredulous noises continues unabated for some time before [Root.Leader.GetSheHe] shakes [Root.Leader.GetHerHis] head, defeated. "It seems this entire facility was cobbled together with duct tape," [Root.Leader.GetSheHe] says. "I'm surprised it ever worked."

descriptions.zh:
我们注意到，这个空间站上大量看似完好的系统似乎都在发生灾难性故障，其频率远超预期——即便考虑到它们的年代也是如此。

在几次艰难的系统重启尝试后，我们的一名维修工[root.GetIndividualNamePlural]发生了严重崩溃："超出理性参数范围，"它开始不停重复这句话。这种状态持续了一段时间，最终[root.GetIndividualName]被迫完全放弃了尝试，让我们不得不得出结论：这个设施的程序设计根本不具备可用性。我们甚至无法理解这个设施曾经是如何正常运转的。
descriptions.en:
We note that a large number of apparently undamaged systems aboard this station seem to be suffering catastrophic failures, far more frequently than expected - even allowing for their age.

Following several arduous attempts to reactivate these systems, one of our repair [root.GetIndividualNamePlural] suffered a critical meltdown: "Context exceeds parameters of reason," it began bleating. This continued for some time before the [root.GetIndividualName] was forced to abandoned the attempt altogether, resigning us to a conclusion that the facility programming is not fit for purpose. We cannot fathom how this facility ever functioned properly.

tooltips.zh: §H敲击维护者§! 以§R-1§!§H技能上限§!为代价，增加§H考古学§!和§H计算§!领域的研究速度。
tooltips.en: §HPercussive Maintainer§! grants faster research in the fields of §HArchaeology§! and §HComputing§! at the cost of §R-1§! max §HSkill Levels§!.

descriptions.zh: 尽管过程经常中断，[Root.Leader.GetName]已在破译该空间站的用途方面取得重大进展。日志表明，它的创造者“鲁达里”一直在与一个被称为“波格-莫里”灭杀种族进行长期斗争——一场他们即将输掉的战争。为了在绝望的最后一搏中扭转局势，一群激进的鲁达里政治家得出结论，保证他们生存的唯一方法是彻底消灭敌人。由于无法通过常规手段击败波格-莫里舰队，他们资助了一个绝密项目，旨在制造一种能够利用恒星的力量在跨恒星系空间发射的激光武器。然而，虽然他们可以在这个问题上投入大量资源，但该项目成立地较为仓促，并且不断有危险发生——无论是被敌人还是被他们自己政府内不愿屈服于此类措施的派系。
descriptions.en: Despite the frequent outages, [Root.Leader.GetName] has been able to make significant progress in deciphering the purpose of the station. Logs indicate that its creators, the "Rudari," had been engaged in a long struggle with a genocidal race known as the "Pogg-Mory" - a war they were losing. In a desperate last-ditch effort to turn the tide, a radical group of Rudari politicians concluded that the only way to guarantee their survival was through the total annihilation of the enemy. Unable to defeat the Pogg-Mory fleet by conventional means, they funded a top secret project to build a laser weapon capable of firing across interstellar space by harnessing the power of a star. However, it appears that while they could throw considerable resources at the problem, the project was hastily set up and in constant danger of discovery - either by the enemy or by factions within their own government unwilling to stoop to such measures.

options.script:
name = ancrel.12010.A
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
[Root.Leader.GetName]发现了鲁达里首席科学官的个人日志，这些日志看起来是一连串对该项目看起来不可能的要求以及迅速下降的质量和安全标准的抱怨。“没有时间测试任何东西，”最后一篇文章中写道。“这是我族人的最后一搏，敌人已经察觉到了我们。我们必须希望到此为止了。他们来了。”

日志表明由于该武器在那不久之后进行测试，所有记录都将停止于此。有证据表明，超级武器仅仅是成功摧毁了空间站。鲁达里似乎将其位置的秘密带到了他们的坟墓中——阻止我们找到他们的遗族。

空间站程序和总体状况都不足以让我们冒险尝试重新启动它并完成这个项目。然而，“死亡激光”中使用的一些创新概念为我们自己的武器专家提供了宝贵的见解。
descriptions.en:
[Root.Leader.GetName] has uncovered the Rudari Chief Science Officer's personal logs, which read as a litany of complaints about the seemingly impossible demands of the project and their rapidly falling quality and safety standards. "There is no time to test anything," reads one of the last entries. "This is the last gambit of my people, and the enemy has our scent. We must hope that this is enough. They are coming."

The logs indicate that the weapon was due to be tested soon after, at which point all records cease. Evidence suggests that the superweapon succeeded only in destroying the station. The Rudari seemingly took the secret of its location to their graves - allowing us to find its remains undisturbed.

Neither the programming nor the general condition of the station are good enough for us to risk trying to reactivate it and complete the project. However, some of the innovative concepts used in the "Death Laser" have provided our own weapons specialists with valuable insights.

descriptions.zh:
我们发现了明显的迹象，迹象表明[From.Planet.GetName]曾经人口稠密。然而，尽管不知道是什么摧毁了他们文明，摧毁都做得非常彻底：几乎没有发现有用的遗骸。

我们的扫描仪在地表深处探测到几个可能曾经支持生命的大洞。也许我们会在那里有更多的运气。
descriptions.en:
We have discovered clear signs that [From.Planet.GetName] was once densely populated. However, whatever destroyed their civilization did a very thorough job of it: very few useful remains have been found.

Our scanners have detected several large cavities deep below the surface that may once have supported life. Perhaps we will have more luck there.

options.script:
name = INTERESTING
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh: 我们对[From.Planet.GetName]上的洞穴系统的挖掘发现了保存完好、规模宏大的地下高科技社会遗迹。许多废墟的状况出奇的好，我们设法找到了[Owner.GetResearchers]所描述的加密数据水晶“图书馆”。希望这些可以对这里发生的事情有所了解。
descriptions.en: Our excavation of the cave systems on [From.Planet.GetName] has found well-preserved remnants of an underground, high technology society built on a vast scale. Many of the ruins are in surprisingly good condition, and we have managed to find what our [Owner.GetResearchers] are describing as a "library" of encrypted data crystals. Hopefully, these can shed some light on what happened here.

options.script:
name = first_contact.5.A
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh: 一个在[FromFrom.Planet.GetName]上探索废墟的[Owner.GetTeamMember]最近失踪了。经过短暂的搜索，我们找到了一具可能属于[Root.Owner.Species.GetName]的[Owner.GetSpeciesRemnantName]。我们的[Owner.GetResearchers]毫不怀疑这些遗骸是我们失踪的[Owner.GetTeamMember]的遗骸，但他们对尸体如何如此迅速地分解感到困惑。他们敦促我们在接下来的调查中保持谨慎。
descriptions.en: A [Owner.GetTeamMember] exploring the ruins on [FromFrom.Planet.GetName] recently disappeared. After a short search, we found a [Owner.GetSpeciesRemnantName] that seems to have belonged to a [Root.Owner.Species.GetName]. Our [Owner.GetResearchers] are in no doubt that these remains are what's left of our missing [Owner.GetTeamMember], but they are baffled about how the body decayed quite this quickly. They urge caution as we continue our investigations.

descriptions.zh: 一个在[FromFrom.Planet.GetName]上探索废墟的[Owner.GetTeamMember]最近失踪了。经过短暂的搜索，我们找到了一具可能属于[Root.Owner.Species.GetName]的[Owner.GetSpeciesRemnantName]。我们的[Owner.GetResearchers]毫不怀疑这些遗骸是我们失踪的[Owner.GetTeamMember]的遗骸，但他们对他们的单元如何如此迅速地腐蚀感到困惑。他们敦促我们在接下来的调查中保持谨慎。
descriptions.en: A [Owner.GetTeamMember] exploring the ruins on [FromFrom.Planet.GetName] recently disappeared. After a short search, we found a [Owner.GetSpeciesRemnantName] that seems to have belonged to a [Root.Owner.Species.GetName]. Our [Owner.GetResearchers] are in no doubt that these remains are what's left of our missing [Owner.GetTeamMember], but they are baffled as to how their unit corroded away quite this quickly. They urge caution as we continue our investigations.

descriptions.zh: 一个在[FromFrom.Planet.GetName]上探索废墟的[Owner.GetTeamMember]最近失踪了。经过短暂的搜索，我们找到了一具可能属于[Root.Owner.Species.GetName]的[Owner.GetSpeciesRemnantName]。我们的[Owner.GetResearchers]毫不怀疑这些遗骸是我们失踪的[Owner.GetTeamMember]的遗骸，但他们对究竟是什么杀死了他们感到困惑——这个过程似乎相当地迅速。他们敦促我们在接下来的调查中保持谨慎。
descriptions.en: A [Owner.GetTeamMember] exploring the ruins on [FromFrom.Planet.GetName] recently disappeared. After a short search, we found a [Owner.GetSpeciesRemnantName] that seems to have belonged to a [Root.Owner.Species.GetName]. Our [Owner.GetResearchers] are in no doubt that these remains are what's left of our missing [Owner.GetTeamMember], but they are baffled as to what exactly killed them - the process seems to have been fairly instantaneous. They urge caution as we continue our investigations.

name = ancrel.2047.a
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
我们解析来自[From.Planet.GetName]洞穴中的数据水晶时，拼凑出了一个陷入困境的星球的景象。

这个星球曾经是一个繁荣的文明的中心，被称为伊兰尼基金会。在那个文明的后期，伊兰尼人越来越倾向于囤积知识，而不关心物质问题，比如生育。结果，他们的人口迅速减少。他们的领袖对他们不断减少的人数感到震惊，他们试图找到永生的技术解决方案。在这一点上，记录变得越来越稀少——尽管它似乎早于迫使他们进入地下的某种灾难——目前尚不清楚他们的努力有什么结果。
descriptions.en:
As we interpret the data crystals from the caves on [From.Planet.GetName], we begin piecing together a picture of a troubled planet.

The planet was once the center of a prosperous civilization known as the Ilanii Foundation. During that civilization's latter years, the Ilanii turned more and more to the hoarding of knowledge instead of more material matters such as procreation. As a result, their population fell rapidly. Alarmed by their dwindling numbers, their leaders attempted to find a technological solution for immortality. Records become scarcer around this point - though it appears to predate whatever cataclysm forced them underground - and it is not clear yet what results their efforts yielded.

descriptions.zh:
我们现在可以拼凑出伊兰尼尝试永生的结果了。看来，他们远没有永生，而是制造了一种可怕的威胁——一群能够快速繁殖并且几乎立即吞噬任何有机物的微生物……就像我们团队失踪成员身上发生过的事情那样。

由此产生的大灾难消灭了大部分人口。幸存者分裂成两组：其中一组，不愿放弃[From.Planet.GetName]，遁入深处，在我们发现的那个密不透风的洞穴中重建他们的文明。然而，从长远来看，这种解决方案被证明是不可持续的，最终微生物找到了进入它们的栖息地的方法。洞穴成了他们的坟墓。

另一组流亡星海，通过彻底摧毁地表使其无法居住的方法来强制执行行星隔离。 从此以后，他们将生活在小飞地中，并致力于保存他们文明中失落的知识，最终演变成现代§H[curator_enclave_country.GetName]§! 的祖先之一。
descriptions.en:
We can now piece together what became of the Ilanii's attempt at immortality. It appears that, far from bringing them everlasting life, they created a terrible menace - a swarm of microorganisms capable of multiplying rapidly and almost instantly devouring any organic matter... as must have happened to our team's lost member.

The resulting cataclysm wiped out much of the population. The survivors splintered into two groups: one, unwilling to give up [From.Planet.GetName], took to the depths, recreating their civilization in air-tight pockets such as the one we found. However, this solution proved unsustainable in the long run, and eventually the microorganism found its way into their habitats; the caves became their tombs.

The other group instead went into exile, enforcing a planetary quarantine by utterly obliterating the surface, rendering it uninhabitable. They would henceforth live in small enclaves and dedicate themselves to preserving the lost knowledge of their civilization, eventually morphing into one of the ancestors of the modern §H[curator_enclave_country.GetName]§!.

label.zh: 这种有机微生物将成为一种很好的武器。
label.en: This microorganism will make a fine weapon.

label.en: All-Devouring Microorganism? Meet a your macro match.

label.en: Quarantine the planet, allowing only careful study.

descriptions.zh:
[From.GetName]恒星系笼罩着诡异的光芒。[Root.GetName]突然出现在星系的某个区域，我们确信这里此前数代人甚至数千年间从未被星系文明造访过。

但等一下，我们的传感器发现了一个能量信号！该信号主要集中在星系中的第一颗行星上，这颗行星似乎不太可能支持生命，毕竟它距离中子星如此接近。但好像还有其他信号正在移动。它们直奔[Root.GetName]而去，武器随时准备开火！
descriptions.en:
An eerie glow lies over the [From.GetName] system. The [Root.GetName] has emerged in a sector of the galaxy surely not visited by any galactic civilization for generations - for millennia... if ever.

But wait - our sensors are reporting energy signatures! Most are concentrated on the first planet of the system, an unlikely candidate for life, considering its proximity to a neutron star. But there are others, mobile ones. They are careening towards the [Root.GetName], weapons charged!

options.script: name = BATTLESTATIONS

descriptions.zh: 我们已经击败了[fromfrom.System.GetName]的防御者。这个恒星系里的景象真是光怪陆离：固态物质几乎不存在，即便是小行星带都残破不堪，就像是被人彻底地开采枯竭了一般。一系列巨型装置按照特定的间距环绕着行星，而信号显示的那一颗孤零零的行星也许是人为制造的。其中释放出了强大的能量信号。如果有什么线索的话一定能在那里找到。
descriptions.en: We have defeated the defenders of [fromfrom.System.GetName]. The system is a curious sight: there is very little solid matter remaining in it - even its asteroid belts have a bedraggled look, as if they have been extensively mined. A series of large installations placed at regular intervals around the star, and there is a single planet that our readings suggest may be artificial in origin. Intense energy signals have been detected emanating from it. If answers are to be found, they will be there.

options.script: name = SPLENDID

descriptions.zh:
目前为止，我们的[Owner.GetResearchers]所能推断的是，这个被他们乌鸦嘴般称为“§Y观测终端§!”的行星上从未有过生命的存在。但其上并不缺活动迹象。地表上有稠密的建筑物，大量人造建筑鳞次栉比地排列在荒芜的基岩上，这些规整的阵列几乎覆盖了行星四分之三的地表。数以亿计的无人机正在对其进行维护，执行的任务从简单的清扫到运行高度复杂的装配线皆包含在内。

然而它们的真正作用目前尚不明确。我们的[Owner.GetResearchers]准备派遣一支队伍下到地表以进行进一步调查。
descriptions.en:
As far as our [Owner.GetResearchers] can tell, there has never been life on the planet they have ominously dubbed the "§YObservation Terminal§!". But there is no shortage of activity. The surface is densely built up, massive artificial structures placed upon the bare bedrock in neat, orderly rows that cover almost three quarters of the planet. Billions of mechanical drones maintain them, performing tasks ranging from menial clean-up to running highly-complex assembly lines.

Their exact purpose remains, however, unclear. Our [Owner.GetResearchers] are preparing to send a team to the surface to investigate further.

options.script:
name = INTERESTING
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
这些机器人对我们的[Owner.GetResearchers]毫不关心，即使从它们的身边路过也继续执行着各自的命令。与这些无人机的一切沟通尝试都失败了，即便是尝试打断他们的工作也毫无收获，这些无人机毫不躲闪直接强行冲撞挡路的[Owner.GetResearchers]，造成了严重的损伤。

打那以后，我们的[Owner.GetResearchers]转而将目光放在操控这些无人机的程序上。通过分析拦截到的信号，我们推断其中有一个主宰一切的系统在操控这些无人机。然而，对其进行解码非常困难，可能很难再有进一步的发现了。
descriptions.en:
As our [Owner.GetResearchers] pass amongst them, the drones on the planet ignore their presence and continue going about their tasks. All efforts to communicate with the drones have failed, and even attempts to disrupt them produced no reactions - the drones simply rode roughshod over the interfering [Owner.GetResearchers], causing serious injury.

Since then, our [Owner.GetResearchers] have shifted their focus to the programs steering the drones. Analysis of intercepted signals suggests there is an overarching system steering them. However, the encryption it uses is extremely sophisticated, and it has proven hard to find out more.

options.script:
name = PECULIAR
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh: 尽管我们的[Owner.GetResearchers]已经难以进一步深入调查这颗行星，但还有一支队伍还在继续研究散布在整个恒星系中的物体阵列。总共约有超过一万个这样的物体，它们大部分是长圆柱体外形的装置，似乎仍在运行，持续不断地向行星发送信号。鉴于它们的形状以及它们似乎无一例外地指向我们星系中的各个点的事实，我们无可避免地得出这是一个出奇巨大的传感器阵列的结论。但它会是由谁建造的呢？
descriptions.en: While our [Owner.GetResearchers] have been unable to make further progress investigating the planet, a team has been investigating the array of objects spread across the system. There are over ten thousand of them, all told. Most of them are long and cylindrical devices that still seem to be operating - they are transmitting a signal towards the planet. Given their shape and the fact that they seem to be without exception pointed towards various points in our galaxy, we cannot escape the conclusion that this is an absurdly huge sensor array. But who could have built it?

options.script:
name = DISTURBING
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh: 在一次大胆的行动中，我们的[Owner.GetResearchers]趁着附近没有其他无人机存在时，成功地向一处无人机主机的接入终端植入了窃听装置。该入侵目前还没有被发现，我们对其的印象是这是一个高度复杂的系统，甚至可能远超我们的网络，但完全没有考虑到自卫的需求。毫无疑问他们认为这些防御舰队的武力吓止就已经非常充分了。尽管如此，我们入侵的这个系统庞大得难以置信，甚至庞大这个词用来描述这个涵盖整颗行星的系统来说都有些苍白无力，所以我们需要一些时间来获取更多信息。
descriptions.en: In a daring move, our [Owner.GetResearchers] managed to implant spyware into an access terminal to the drones' mainframe in a moment while no drones were nearby. The intrusion does not appear to have been detected yet. Our impression is of a highly sophisticated system - beyond even our own networks, probably - but one which did not anticipate the need to protect itself. No doubt the physical deterrence of the defense fleet was deemed sufficient. Nevertheless, the systems we are infiltrating are vast - a term which seems a gross understatement for this planetary system - so it will take some time to find out more.

options.script:
name = KEEP_SEARCHING
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
位于极域警哨的自动化系统似乎比我们所能想象的还要古老。我们黑入这个系统取得了数据，可是其中并没有能够帮助我们确认其建造者身份或最终意图的信息。关于系统的建造者，我们唯一可以确定的事情就是他们至少在12亿年前就已经来到了这里，在建造完系统并将其设定为监测整个星系的观测站后就离开了。

值得一提的是，经历如此漫长的岁月后，这个系统仍在运作。遍布整个系统的装置阵列实际上是高度精密的传感器，它们会向该星球发送实时数据，而在星球上的中央处理系统则会将这些数据转化为无人机可以保存并长期存储的数据。由于受到存储空间与物资短缺的影响，他们似乎下决心改进了数据压缩技术。这个星球上的巨型结构自称其存储了自建造以来的所有观测数据，不过我们却无法证实这一点，毕竟这些数据被过度压缩，已经超出我们的解压能力了。

令人不安的是，尽管发送频率下降，但其依旧在向外界广播“重点”数据流。不过都过了这么久了，应该也没人在监听了吧？不管怎样，我们已经准备好程序接管这些无人机，只要有胆量，我们马上就可以根据我们自己的设想改造这个系统。
descriptions.en:
It seems the automated systems in Ultima Vigilis are older than we can imagine. The data systems we have hacked do not give us any clues as to the identity or ultimate intentions of its creators, but the one thing we have managed to ascertain is that they arrived no less than 1.2 billion years ago, and departed soon after setting up the system as an observation post to surveil our entire galaxy.

Remarkably, the system is still operating even after all these years: the array of installations spread across the system are, it turns out, highly sophisticated sensors. They send a live feed to the planet, where the central operating system processes it into information the drones can save and store. Spurred on by shortages of space and matter, it appears that they have improved their data compression techniques with determination: the massive structures on the planet purport to contain the sum of all observations ever recorded. However, we cannot test this assertion, since the data is compressed well beyond our ability to decompress it.

Disturbingly, a reduced stream of "highlights" is still being broadcast into empty space. But surely no one is still listening, after all this time? Regardless, our programs are poised to take control of the drones. We may now shape the system to our imagination - if we dare.

label.zh: 我们可以将这一整颗星球整合进我们自己的操作系统。
label.en: We can integrate the world into our own operating system.

label.zh: 让它们继续，我们可以提取他们的数据。
label.en: Let them continue - we can siphon off their readings.

label.en: Distribute the drones to our colonies.

label.zh: 这个运作良好的网络可以为我们所用。
label.en: A well-organized network such as this could serve us well.

descriptions.zh: 在勾陈一的最后一个侵略者倒下后，我们的舰船在返回港口之前完成了对恒星系的最后一次扫描，并发现了一些奇怪的东西。在勾陈一 II 的星球上，我们的传感器显示有重金属被排列成了人造结构。有趣的是，这些构造中中似乎只有一个漂浮在行星海洋上，而其余的则在海面以下。我们怀疑这是外星生命的杰作。
descriptions.en: After the last of the aggressors in Polaris fell, our ships completed a final scan of the system before heading back to port and discovered something curious. On the world of Polaris II, heavy metals are arranged in artificial structures on our sensors. Interestingly only one of these formations appears to be floating on the planetary ocean while the rest are below the surface. We suspect this is the work of alien life.

options.script: name = CURIOUS

descriptions.zh:
漂浮的冰山本身内置了一个巨大的黑色长方体，由与上方太空舰队残骸相同的合金制成。我们的冰川专家表示，尽管据称“很难用外星大气来判断”，冰山形成依然可以追溯到至少一千年前。结构内部的扫描显示有相当多的生物读数，因此不建议使用破坏性工具。

团队将不得不穿越冰冻的悬崖，到达似乎是建筑物入口的地方。
descriptions.en:
Built into the floating iceberg itself is a hulking black cuboid made out of the same alloys as the wreckage of the space fleet above. Our glacial specialists state that analysis of the iceberg dates its formation to least a thousand years ago, though it's supposedly "hard to tell with alien atmospheres". Scans of the interior of the structure show quite a few biological readings, therefore using disruptive tools is inadvisable.

The team will have to traverse the frozen cliffs to what appears to be an entrance into the building.

options.script:
name = acnrel.13005.a
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh: 我们在[From.Planet.GetName]的设施入口处建立了大本营。我们已经发现了一些看起来像是刻在建筑物墙壁上的文字。现在我们将开始在不会损坏里面任何东西的情况下打开这扇门的漫长而艰巨的过程。与此同时，我们的异种语言学家尝试翻译铭文中已失传的外星语言。
descriptions.en: We have set up base camp at the supposed entrance to the facility here on [From.Planet.GetName]. Already we have discovered something that looks like writing inscribed on the walls of the building. Now we will begin the long and arduous process of opening this door without damaging whatever is inside. At the same time, our xeno-linguists attempt to translate the dead alien language of the inscriptions.

options.script:
name = INTERESTING
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh: 是时候了，我们已经准备好解封黑色结构，根据墙上铭文的初步翻译，它被称为“避难所”。这个避难所的创造者勾陈一星人将其作为保护财宝安全的最后手段。当我们打开门时，迎接我们的是——根据我们的传感器的数据——一种类似于外界空气的受控大气，只是二氧化碳要少得多。
descriptions.en: The time was upon us, and we stood ready to unseal the black structure, dubbed "The Vault" according to preliminary translations of the wall inscriptions. The creators of this vault, the Polarians, made it as a last resort to keep their treasures safe. As we opened the doors, we were greeted by - according to our sensors - a controlled atmosphere similar to the air outside, just with quite a bit less carbon dioxide.

options.script:
name = EXCELLENT

descriptions.zh:
远古种子！植物胚胎——那是勾陈一星人藏在这个金库里的宝藏。进一步的翻译告诉我们，这些外星人怪异地不断用过量二氧化碳填充他们的大气层。一旦气候发生不可逆转的变化，这个星球的古代居民就会收集他们所能找到的所有不能在新环境下生存的植物物质，并将它们全部冻结在这里。

那时，整个星球都会被冰覆盖；现在，只剩下这片孤独的小冰山了。然而，他们的努力不会白费——拿到星球上的整个植物生态的编目和分类，将极大地帮助我们的科学家研究未来的生物问题。
descriptions.en:
Ancient seeds! Plant embryos - that was the treasure the Polarians hid away in this vault. Further translations tell us that these aliens curiously kept filling their atmosphere with too much carbon dioxide. Once the atmosphere was irreversibly changed the ancient inhabitants of this world gathered all the plant matter they could find that might not survive their new status quo and froze them all in here.

Back then, the whole planet would have been covered in ice; now, all that remains is this small lonely iceberg. However, their efforts will not have been wasted - having a planet's whole plant ecology already cataloged and sorted will significantly help our scientists in researching future biological matters.

descriptions.zh:
有机微生物！所有有害和有益的细菌。所有真核生物和原核生物。所有这些都在高级存储设施中标记和分类：这是勾陈一星人藏在这个金库中的巨大财富。进一步的翻译告诉我们，这些外星人怪异地不断用过量二氧化碳填充他们的大气层。一旦大气发生了不可逆转的变化，这个星球的古代居民就会收集他们所能找到的所有不能在新环境下生存的微生物，并将它们全部冻结在这里。

那时，整个星球都会被冰覆盖；现在，只剩下这片孤独的小冰山了。然而，他们的努力不会白费——拿到星球的整个微生物生态的编目和分类，将极大地帮助我们的[Root.Owner.getscientistplural]开发新星球以及改造殖民地。
descriptions.en:
Microorganisms! Every harmful and helpful bacterium. Every eukaryote and prokaryote. All in an advanced storage facility labeled and cataloged: this was the great treasure the Polarians hid away in this vault. Further translations tell us that these aliens curiously kept filling their atmosphere with too much carbon dioxide. Once the atmosphere was irreversibly changed, the ancient inhabitants of this world gathered all the microbial life they could find that might not survive their new status quo and froze them all in here.

Back then, the whole planet would have been covered in ice; now, all that remains is this small lonely iceberg. However, their efforts will not have been wasted - having a planet's whole microbial ecology already cataloged and sorted will significantly help our [Root.Owner.getscientistplural] develop new and improved colonies for new worlds.
