descriptions.zh:
在[From.Planet.GetName]上发现了充满蘑菇的巨大峡谷，这就是答案的开始。原来水在这些蘑菇里面。它们似乎扩张到了星球表面的很大一部分，并且都与同一个菌丝体相连，因此从技术上讲，它算是一个单一的有机体，也是我们见过的最大的有机体之一。该团队的一些成员将这种巨大的真菌称为“巨大蘑菇”。

看起来蘑菇已经过基因改造，并完全接管了曾经存在于这里的生态系统。它们肆无忌惮地加速生长，以至于它们吸收了这里存在的大部分水。随后，它们进入了一种干枯的休眠状态，在这种状态下，大部分真菌仍然活着，水遍布整个生物体。
descriptions.en:
The discovery on [From.Planet.GetName] of vast canyons filled with mushrooms provided us with the beginning of an answer. The water is inside the mushrooms. They seem to span a large part of the surface of the world, all connected to the same mycelium, which technically makes it a single organism, and one of the biggest we've ever seen. Some of the members of the team dubbed this humongous fungus the 'Fumongus'.

It looks like the mushrooms have been genetically altered and have completely taken over the ecosystem that once existed here. Their unbridled and accelerated growth was such that they absorbed most of the water that was present here. They subsequently entered a sort of dried-up dormant state in which most of the fungus is still alive, with water spread out across the whole organism.

descriptions.zh:
在坐落在[From.Planet.GetName]峡谷中的菌丝森林的深处，我们发现了某种地堡，早已被蘑菇摧垮。该团队认为，它是由对这里的蘑菇进行基因改造的那个物种建造的。

地堡的大部分已经倒塌，其中的许多设备可能已经损坏无法修复，但我们已经确定了一些可能装有可利用材料的密封房间。值得注意的是，这里没有发现外星人遗骸。也许他们放弃了这个地方，也或者全部被当地野生动物所吸收了。
descriptions.en:
Deep in the heart of the mycelial forests nestled in the canyons of [From.Planet.GetName] we discovered some sort of bunker, long overrun by mushrooms. The team believes that it was built by the same species that genetically altered the mushrooms here. 

Large sections of the bunker have collapsed and a lot of the equipment within it is likely broken beyond repair, but we have identified some sealed rooms that might hold exploitable material. Notably, no alien remains have been found here. Maybe they abandoned the place, or else didn't leave behind any body parts that weren't absorbed by the local wildlife.

descriptions.zh:
[From.Planet.GetName]上的地堡用于保护计算设备，其中一些似乎直接连接到菌丝体。值得庆幸的是，我们设法重新激活了几个终端和数据库。

破解加密和解密所使用的语言需要时间，团队已要求派我们的几位顶级[Root.Owner.GetLinguists]来帮忙。
descriptions.en:
The bunker on [From.Planet.GetName] was used to protect computing equipment, some of which appears to be directly connected to the mycelium. Thankfully, we managed to reactivate several terminals and databanks.

Breaking the encryption and deciphering the language used will take time, and the team has requested that several of our top [Root.Owner.GetLinguists] be sent here to help.

descriptions.zh:
我们从[From.Planet.GetName]地堡中的数据库中找到了有价值的信息。数据库告诉我们，这是一种监听哨站。显然，外星人找到了一种方法来解释通过菌丝体传播的信号并将它们转化为可操作的情报。

我们不明白这怎么实现的，但该团队现在将尝试从附近的冰小行星带运水过来再次“唤醒”巨大蘑菇，看看如果它有传输数据的话，传输的是什么样的数据。
descriptions.en:
We have recovered valuable information from the databanks found in the bunker on [From.Planet.GetName]. The databanks tell us that this was a sort of listening post. Apparently, the aliens found a way to interpret the signals coursing through the mycelium and convert them into actionable intel.

We do not understand how this might have been possible, but the team will now try to bring water from nearby ice asteroids to 'awaken' the Fumongus again and see what kind data it transmits, if any.

descriptions.zh:
[From.Planet.GetName]上的蘑菇又开始繁茂了。在其他几艘飞船的帮助下，我们不得不将几颗冰小行星拖入轨道，然后将其中的大块降落到行星上的各个地方进行融化。这是一个漫长的过程，但它终于开始有结果了。

有了这个，计算机开始吐出看起来非常随机的小块数据，直到我们从母星上分辨出信号。与[Root.Owner.Capital.GetName]的团队进行了一系列合作实验，唯一可能的结论是蘑菇对其他星球上发生的事情的有有限的了解。虽然我们检索到的数据尚不可利用，但预计继续尝试恢复蘑菇会给我们带来更多结果。
descriptions.en:
The mushrooms on [From.Planet.GetName] are starting to flourish again. With the help of several other ships, we had to tow several icy asteroids into orbit before bringing down chunks of them to various places on the planet to melt. It has been long process, but it is finally beginning to bear fruit.

With this, the computers began to spit out small bits of data that seemed pretty random until we recognized activity from our home. In cooperation with teams on [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName], a series of experiments has been conducted and the only possible conclusion is that the mushroom has some limited awareness of what happens on other planets. While the data we have retrieved is not exploitable just yet, continued efforts to restore the mushrooms are expected to give us more results.

descriptions.zh:
菌丝体监听阵列终于可以运行了。已经从轨道上带来了大量的水来满足一直很渴的蘑菇，并且对计算资源进行了重大升级。

仍然存在一些谜团，毕竟我们仍然不确定蘑菇是如何设法从星系其他地方收集这么多数据的。考虑到所传达的信息量，穿越网络的信号数量出人意料地低。最重要的理论假设巨大蘑菇存在于跨维度，在这些维度的距离与我们的习惯不同。
在任何情况下，巨大蘑菇都可以与它跨越星系的后代接触，这些较小的殖民地能够传递数据，我们可以解析这些数据。

随着网络再次运行，剩下的唯一决议就是是否将其用于监视。
descriptions.en:
The Mycelium Listening Array is finally operational. A significant supply of water has been brought from orbit to sate the ever-thirsty mushroom, and major upgrades have been made to the computing resources.

Some mysteries remain, as we are still not sure how the mushroom manages to collect that much data from the rest of the galaxy. The number of signals traversing the network proved surprisingly low, considering the quantity of information conveyed. The most prominent theory posits that the Fumongus exists across dimensions where distances are not what we are used to.
In any case, the Fumongus is in contact with its offspring across the galaxy, and these smaller colonies are able to relay data, which we can then interpret.

With the network working again, the only decision left to make is whether to use it for surveillance, or not.

label.zh: 能监听还能汇报。也许我们也可以学学类似的事情。
label.en: Monitor and report. Perhaps we can learn something similar.

descriptions.zh:
菌丝体监听阵列终于可以运行了。已经从轨道上带来了大量的水来满足一直很渴的蘑菇，并且对计算资源进行了重大升级。

然而，关于菌丝网络，我们仍然知之甚少。考虑到所传达的信息量，穿越网络的信号数量出人意料地低。最重要的理论假设巨大蘑菇存在于跨维度，在这些维度的距离与我们的习惯不同。
在任何情况下，巨大蘑菇都可以与它跨越星系的后代接触，这些较小的殖民地能够传递数据，我们可以解析这些数据。 但是还有谁可以访问这个网络呢？有很多数据我们无法与这个星系中的恒星系相关联。我们更悲观的 [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] 认为我们可能不是唯一在倾听的人，通过重新激活网络，我们只是向使用它的所有人展示了我们自己。

鉴于我们仍然不了解巨大蘑菇，以及之前接触过它的物种，最好不要管它。
descriptions.en:
The Mycelium Listening Array is finally operational. A significant supply of water has been brought from orbit to sate the ever-thirsty mushroom, and major upgrades have been made to the computing resources.

And yet, there is still so much we don't know about the mycelial network.  The number of signals traversing the network proved surprisingly low, considering the quantity of information conveyed. The most prominent theory posits that the Fumongus exists across dimensions where distances are not what we are used to.
In any case, the Fumongus is in contact with its offspring across the galaxy, and these smaller colonies are able to relay data, which we can then interpret. But who else may have access to this network? There is a lot of data that we were not able to correlate to systems in this galaxy. Our more pessimistic [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] argue we might not be the only ones listening, and that by reactivating the network we just revealed ourselves to anyone using it.

Given all we still don't know about the Fumongus, or about the previous species that tapped into it, it might be best to just leave it alone..

label.zh: 偏执的傻瓜。我们该使用它。
能监听还能汇报。也许我们也可以学学类似的事情。
label.en: Monitor and report. Perhaps we can learn something similar.

descriptions.zh: 当我们打开这艘外星人星舰的气阀门时，等待在另一边的是一片修罗地狱。我们初步调查发现，这里简直就是一片残杀现场。在检查支离破碎的船员尸体之后，我们很确定他们生前正互相撕扯对方的四肢。我们可以转身就走……但那样我们就永远没法发现这场悲剧是怎么发生的了。
descriptions.en: When we opened the airlock of the alien starship, putrefaction and decay awaited us on the other side. Our preliminary investigation has uncovered a scene of carnage. After examining the mutilated bodies of the crew, we are certain they tore each other limb from limb. We could just leave... but then we'd never know why this tragedy happened.

descriptions.zh: 随着进一步的发掘，我们找到了这艘船的科学实验室。微弱的能量布满这片区域，泛出轻柔的紫外光。一片凌乱的紫色灌木正在厚重的孢子云。看来，这艘船的医生利用实验室和通风闸将一片有毒的云雾排放到了飞船的每一个角落。
descriptions.en: Digging deeper, we have uncovered the ship's science lab. Minimal power saturates the scene in ultraviolent illumination. A riot of purple shrubbery is releasing thick clouds of spores. The ship's doctor used a laboratory and ventilation shafts to flood the ship with an intoxicating mist.

options.script:

descriptions.zh: 我们认为自己能免疫这片有毒云雾带来的危害。如果我们能让飞船的引擎运作起来，我们就能启动这艘船并将其送回母星研究。这需要时间，但这座精密的药学实验室能为我们帝国的士兵们提供有用的生物增强剂。
descriptions.en: We think we are immune to the full effects of the intoxicating mist. If we can get the ship's engines online, we can launch the ship and send it back home for study. This will take time, but the elaborate pharmaceutical laboratory may provide useful biochemical augmentation for our empire's soldiers.

label.zh: 运行诊断程序，并开始修复。

descriptions.zh: 我们愚蠢地以为我们能够免疫这片云雾，但是我们的工程师们已经陷入了销魂极乐的状态。他们在飞船的过道跳舞，大声地唱歌。我们需要时间对空气进行净化，抓住这帮子工程师，然后才能发动飞船。这些耽搁会花费我们的时间。
descriptions.en: We foolishly thought we were immune to the mist, but our engineers are experiencing a state of rapturous bliss. They dance in the ship's corridors, singing atonally. We will need to clear the atmosphere and capture our engineers before we can launch the ship. This delay will cost us time.

label.zh: 抓住已经陷入“极乐”的工程师。

descriptions.zh: 我们起飞了！尽管很危险，但外星人飞船的有毒迷雾确实能够增强我们帝国士兵的战斗力和忠诚心。然而，问题还是存在：我们应该让自己的士兵去接触这种有害的物质吗？或者我们从这场悲剧的错误中学得教训，放弃这一切？
descriptions.en: We have liftoff! Though dangerous, the alien ship's intoxicating mist could augment the effectiveness and loyalty of our empire's soldiers. However, the question remains: should we subject our own soldiers to this hazardous substance? Or should we say no and learn from their tragic mistakes?

label.zh: 好好利用这个令人惊叹的科技。

tooltips.zh: 胜利在等着！我们的士兵应该愿意冒这个风险。
tooltips.en: Victory awaits! Our soldiers should be willing to take this risk.

tooltips.zh: 有些秘密我们还是别知道为好。
tooltips.en: There are some secrets we were not meant to know.

descriptions.zh:
我们实在是很难说[From.Planet.GetName]到底算不算作一个行星：初步钻探发现的是一层又一层的生物组织。据估计，总共需要2,435,463只缇扬奇尸体才能产生此等规模的行星质量（误差范围5.3%）。即使我们假设地核是一块岩石，尸体只是堆叠在上面，涉及到的样本数量依然是无比庞大的。

是某人或者某种事物将缇扬奇带到这里让它们死去，还是说它们只是顺其自然地来到这里度过最后的时光，然后死去？
descriptions.en:
It's hard to determine if [From.Planet.GetName] is even a planet: preliminary drilling has only revealed strata upon strata of biological tissue. According to estimations, it would take 2,435,463 Tiyanki bodies to produce a planetary mass of this size (with a margin of error equal to 5.3%). Even assuming the existence of a rocky core upon which the corpses are layered, the number of specimens involved is still significant.

Did someone or something bring the Tiyanki here to die, or are they naturally drawn to this place as their final hour draws near?

descriptions.zh:
我们实在是很难说[From.Planet.GetName]到底算不算作一个行星：初步钻探发现的是一层又一层的生物组织。据估计，总共需要2,435,463只缇扬奇尸体才能产生此等规模的行星质量（误差范围5.3%）。即使我们假设地核是一块岩石，尸体只是堆叠在上面，涉及到的样本数量依然是无比庞大的。

是某人或者某种事物将缇扬奇带到这里让它们死去，还是说它们只是顺其自然地来到这里度过最后的时光，然后死去？最重要的是：为什么我们的死灵法师不能复活它们？为什么这堆死去的肉体拒绝我们，就好像已经有其他存在在控制它们一样？
descriptions.en:
It's hard to determine if [From.Planet.GetName] is even a planet: preliminary drilling has only revealed strata upon strata of biological tissue. According to estimations, it would take 2,435,463 Tiyanki bodies to produce a planetary mass of this size (with a margin of error equal to 5.3%). Even assuming the existence of a rocky core upon which the corpses are layered, the number of specimens involved is still significant.

Did someone or something bring the Tiyanki here to die, or are they naturally drawn to this place as their final hour draws near? Most crucially: why are our Necromancers unable to revive them? Why does this dead flesh reject us, as if already controlled by another entity?

descriptions.zh:
遍布[From.Planet.GetName]地表的死亡缇扬奇的那种不寻常……的活动，似乎是它们再生能力的一种副作用：即使技术上已经判定为死亡，它们的尸体仍旧在不断地重组再生。这个恒星系拥有着非比寻常般丰富的营养物质，尤其是缇扬奇游荡的那个气态巨行星。或许这解释了为什么我们之前从未观察到这样的行为。

然而，这个发现并没有解释为什么这些死去的生物像是在被某种单一思维控制一样蠕动，不断地伸出触手，吞食新近降落到这个行星上的尸体。

我们希望进一步的挖掘能够揭示这个地方，或这个生命……的内在运作规律，带给我们新的见解。我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]还在就术语和分类问题无法达成一致。
descriptions.en:
The unusual... liveliness of the dead Tiyanki covering the surface of [From.Planet.GetName] seems to be a byproduct of their regenerative capabilities: even if technically dead, the bodies are still reassembling themselves. This system is unusually rich in nourishing substances typically found in the gas giants where Tiyanki graze. Perhaps that explains why this behavior hasn't been observed before.

This discovery does not explain why the dead seem to move as if controlled by a single mind, extending their tentacles to encroach upon the new carcasses falling on the planet.

Further excavations will hopefully reveal new insights on the inner workings of this... place. Or being. Our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] are still divided on the exact nomenclature.

descriptions.zh: 我们的挖掘队发掘到了一个复杂的隧道网络，从[From.Planet.GetName]的地表一直延伸到地下深处。化学分析确认迷宫的墙体是由压实的缇扬奇组织构成，尽管其年代甚至超过了我们的帝国，但肉质还散发着温热，甚至几乎没有腐败。看上去就像是这些尸体自己聚合到了一起，重构其形态建立了这个地方……但是为什么？
descriptions.en: Our excavations unearthed a complex network of tunnels extending under the surface of [From.Planet.GetName]. Chemical analysis confirms the walls are entirely composed of highly compressed Tiyanki tissue, the flesh still warm and hardly decomposed despite rivaling the age of our empire. It's as if the corpses were fused together, reshaped and modified to form this place... But why?

descriptions.zh:
在对[From.Planet.GetName]的地下隧道网络进行测绘的时候，我们[Owner.GetScientistPlural]突然意识到，这个隧道网络同一只缇扬奇的血管系统极其相似——但是其规模达到了行星级别。

那些搏动的墙壁散发着轻微的温暖，随着探险队逐渐接近行星的核心，墙壁的温度也在慢慢提升——在核心处，我们的扫描仪捕捉到了一个微弱的生命信号。
descriptions.en:
After mapping the extensive underground network of [From.Planet.GetName], our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] realized the tunnels closely match the structure of the Tiyanki vascular system - but on a planetary scale.

The pulsating walls emanate a soft warmth, the temperature slowly increasing as the expedition approached the planet core - where our scanners have picked up a faint life signal.

descriptions.zh:
在对[From.Planet.GetName]的地下隧道网络进行测绘的时候，我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]突然意识到，这个隧道网络同一只缇扬奇的血管系统极其相似——但是其规模跟我们之前遇到的那只在星辰间游荡的缇扬奇族母差不多。

那些搏动的墙壁散发着轻微的温暖，随着探险队逐渐接近行星的核心，墙壁的温度也在慢慢提升——在核心处，我们的扫描仪捕捉到了一个微弱的生命信号。
descriptions.en:
After mapping the extensive underground network of [From.Planet.GetName], our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] realized the tunnels closely match the structure of the Tiyanki vascular system - but on a scale comparable to that of the Tiyanki Matriarch we encountered while roaming the stars.

The pulsating walls emanate a soft warmth, the temperature slowly increasing as the expedition approached the planet core - where our scanners have picked up a faint life signal.

descriptions.zh:
在一个庞大的地下穴室中，一只缇扬奇竖立地站着，钟型的脑袋微微地摇晃着，它细线一样的触手舒展开来，连接着穴室的外墙。看上去它成为了某种控制单元，不断操纵、指引着这个行星级别墓地的生长。

我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]没法断定什么种类的生物会从如此恐怖的过程中诞生，但是当它苏醒的时候，有一件事是很明确的：它会成为远比普通的缇扬奇要大得多，也恐怖得多的存在。
descriptions.en:
In a vast underground chamber, a Tiyanki stands upright, bell-shaped head swaying lightly, its wiry tentacles spread across the floor to connect with the outer walls of the chamber. It appears to be some sort of command unit, controlling and directing the growth of this planet-sized graveyard.

Our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] are unable to determine what kind of creature will arise from this grim process, and when it will awaken, but one thing is for sure: it will be something far, far more vast and terrible than an ordinary Tiyanki.

在一个庞大的地下穴室中，一只缇扬奇竖立地站着，钟型的脑袋微微地摇晃着，它细线一样的触手舒展开来，连接着穴室的外墙。看上去它成为了某种控制单元，不断操纵、指引着这个行星级别墓地的生长。

我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]没法断定这个过程什么时候会完成，但是相信一旦这只生物苏醒，它会成为远比普通的缇扬奇要大得多，也恐怖得多的存在：这只生物值得我们视作一只新的§H缇扬奇族母§!。

In a vast underground chamber, a Tiyanki stands upright, bell-shaped head swaying lightly, its wiry tentacles spread across the floor to connect with the outer walls of the chamber. It appears to be some sort of command unit, controlling and directing the growth of this planet-sized graveyard.

Our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] don't know when the process will be concluded, but believe once the creature awakens, it will be something far, far more vast and terrible than an ordinary Tiyanki: something worthy of being called a new §HTiyanki Matriarch§!.

label.zh: 在不伤害它的前提下监视其生长。
label.en: Monitor its growth without harming it.

label.zh: 让这个神圣的生命体在和平中成长吧。
label.en: Let this sacred life-form growth in peace.

label.zh: 策展人肯定愿意为这个标本付个好价钱。
label.en: The Curators will pay a good price for this specimen.

descriptions.zh: 在一个庞大的地下穴室中，一只缇扬奇竖立地站着，钟型的脑袋微微地摇晃着，它细线一样的触手舒展开来，连接着穴室的外墙。看上去它成为了某种控制单元，不断操纵、指引着这个行星级别墓地的生长。但是这个生物现在已经死了，被我们用来前往这个地方的挖掘设备毁灭了。核心周边的外壳变得苍白而易碎，整个地方经历了第二次死亡。
descriptions.en: In a vast underground chamber, a Tiyanki stands upright, bell swaying lightly, its wiry tentacles spread on the floor to connect with the outer walls of the chamber. It appeared to be some sort of control unit, controlling and directing the growth of the grave mound. But the creature is now dead, destroyed by the mining equipment we used to get access to this same place. The shells around the core are pallid and brittle; soon, this whole place will die a second death.

descriptions.zh:
我们探险队的一名成员在探索隧道的时候突然消失了。搜寻小队花了好几天时间试图定位[Owner.GetScientist]，结果发现这人被一堵墙给包裹住，身体被触手死死地缠住。

把[Owner.GetScientist]解救出来花费了不少时间和精力。[Owner.GetScientist]并不只是被简单地缠住了：这堵墙正试图在分子层面将[Owner.GetScientist]融合，使其成为墙体表面的一部分。

现在[Owner.GetScientist]的状态稳定了下来，但此人拒绝离开我们的科研船——即使是在那里，也在用极度怀疑的状态死死地盯着墙壁，生怕还会有下一次袭击。
descriptions.en:
A member of our expedition team disappeared while exploring a tunnel. The retrieval squad spent days trying to locate the [Owner.GetScientist], only to find them partly encased in a wall, body tightly wrapped in tentacles.

Freeing the [Owner.GetScientist] took considerable time and effort. The [Owner.GetScientist] was not simply tied: the wall was trying to fuse with the [Owner.GetScientist] at a molecular level, turning them into a part of the surface.

The [Owner.GetScientist] is now in stable condition, but refuses to leave our science ship - and even there, they keep watching the walls with extreme suspicion as though fearing another attack.

label.zh: 获取生物质的一种有趣途径。
label.en: An intriguing way to acquire biomatter.

descriptions.zh:
我们的科学家在[From.Planet.GetName]发现了一些奇怪的东西。作为一颗热带星球，其表面大片区域被茂密的丛林覆盖：巨大的、寿达千年的古树从林冠中突兀而起，它们枝叶茂密的树冠俯瞰着其他陆上景观。

初看起来，这些参天大树的分布似乎杂乱无章。然而，更详细的分析表明这些树的分布具有数学精准性，也许是由某个消失已久的文明所种植的。不仅如此，团队领袖相信，树木的分布方式可能包含着一组坐标，指向丛林深处某个未被探索的区域。
descriptions.en:
Our scientists have discovered something unusual on [From.Planet.GetName]. A tropical world, much of the planet's surface is covered with dense jungle: massive, thousand year old trees erupt from the canopy, their leafy crowns towering over the landscape.

At first glance, the distribution of these giants appears random. However, further analysis indicates that the trees are arranged with mathematical precision, and it seems likely they were planted by some long-vanished civilization. What's more, the team leader believes the distribution pattern may comprise a set of coordinates, one that points to an unexplored location deep within the jungle.

descriptions.zh:
由于[From.Planet.GetName]的林冠非常茂密难以穿透，从空中对穿越丛林便捷路线的搜索几乎一无所获。林冠之下生机勃勃：有无附肢的掠食者、耷拉脸的灵长类和成群的吸血昆虫。森林的土层非常肥沃，而恶臭的水洼让探索团队难以前行。不仅如此，还有某些东西，不知道是茂密的植被还是未知的电磁干扰，使仪器设备经常发生故障。

项目领队相信他们还是能够在树木间找到通路，只是进程可能会非常缓慢。
descriptions.en:
Given the impenetrable canopy on [From.Planet.GetName], aerial surveys have proven useless in determining a convenient route through the jungle. Below, the undergrowth teems with life: limbless predators; droop-faced primates; swarms of hematophagous insects. The forest floor is loamy, and pools of fetid water have caused the team significant delays. What's more, something - either the density of the foliage or an as yet undefined electrical interference - has prevented much of their equipment from functioning properly.

The project's lead believes they should still be able to forge a path through the trees, though progress is likely to be slow.

descriptions.zh:
对土壤的分析显示，[From.Planet.GetName]在过去的一百个公转周期内进行过一场令人惊奇的气候转变。和今天植被茂密的景象大不相同，这颗星球曾经荒芜又遍地岩石。项目领队相信这些巨大的植物本身就是原因：共振显像扫描发现，它们的树汁中存在灵能。这些能量从地下水中被植被巨大的根系抽出，并经由类似光合作用的过程逐渐散布到整个行星的大气中。这很可能就是团队仪器设备出故障的原因。

有趣的是，月光似乎能促进灵能扩散。在晴朗的夜晚，甚至空气看起来都在震颤，这个现象在团队接近目的地的过程中越来越强烈。这一景象我们前所未见。
descriptions.en:
A soil analysis reveals that [From.Planet.GetName] has undergone a startling climatological transformation within its last 100 cycles. Far from the lush jungle world that exists today, the planet was once rocky and barren. The project lead believes the great trees themselves are responsible: a resonance imaging scan detected the presence of psionic energy within their sap. Pulled from groundwater by the trees' vast root systems, this energy is eventually diffused throughout the planet's atmosphere in a process akin to photosynthesis. It is highly likely that this is the cause of the team's malfunctioning equipment.

Interestingly, the presence of moonlight appears to accelerate the psionic diffusion. On clear nights, the air itself seems to vibrate, a phenomenon that has only grown in intensity as the team nears its destination. This is unlike anything we've ever seen before.

descriptions.zh:
在终于抵达他们寻找的坐标后，考古团队发现了一条隐藏在林冠下蜿蜒崎岖的河谷。河水从圆环形的洞口奔流而出，显然，这条河一定发源自某个庞大的地下泉。一条数千年前在岩壁上开凿出来的摇摇欲坠的阶梯将团队带向了一个地下隧道。

洞穴的墙壁和顶上密密麻麻地涂写着一些潦草的象形文字，其中最引人注目的是一个圆形的类人脸的符号。我们的翻译算法成功地解码了许多这类符号，其中这一符号指代这颗星球的卫星。

在洞穴中，灵能的存在已经爆表了。不幸的是，道路的尽头被一处数世纪历史的塌方所封堵，只要稍给一些时间，探险队应该可以设法通过。
descriptions.en:
At last reaching their tracked coordinates, the archaeology team discovered a winding river valley hidden beneath the canopy. Rushing forth from a circular cave-mouth, the river apparently stems from some massive, underground spring. A precarious stairway, carved from the rocks several thousand years ago, delivered the team to a subterranean tunnel.

The cave's walls and ceiling are covered in a compact scrawl of ideographs, the most prominent of which is a round, humanoid face. Our translation algorithms have succeeded in decoding much of the symbology, and this particular image likely represents the planet's moon.

Within the cave, the presence of psionic energy is off the charts. Unfortunately, the path ahead was blocked by a cave-in several centuries ago, but given time, the expedition should be able to find a way through.

descriptions.zh: [From.Planet.GetName]上的科学团队发来了一封喜报！成功进入洞穴下层后，他们最终抵达了一个开阔的、半球形的石室。在这里，河道围绕着一座小小的岛屿流淌，小岛的中央是一块稀有晶体构成的石笋。这座石笋是由数百万年的水滴逐渐形成的，而它似乎就是整颗行星奇异灵能的源头。研究团队发现了宗教仪式的痕迹，还有若干仪式性的人造小祭器散布在石笋支柱的周围。除此之外，多相位扫描还在支柱的地基中发现了一个圆形的物体。一旦挖掘出来，这个物体有很大希望能够提供一些关于这个神秘地方的本质的线索。
descriptions.en: A note of triumph from our science team on [From.Planet.GetName]! After successfully reaching the lower levels of the cave, they at last arrived in a wide, hemispherical chamber. There, the river parts around a small island, at the center of which is a stalagmite of rare crystals. Formed drop-by-drop over the course of several millennia, the pillar appears to be the source of the planet's strange, psionic energy. The team has discovered evidence of religious ritual, as well as several small artifacts of ceremonial significance scattered around the pillar. What's more, a multiphasic scan revealed a round object embedded in the pillar's base. Hopes are high that, once removed, this artifact will shed some light on the true nature of this mysterious place.

descriptions.zh:
[From.Planet.GetName]上传来了坏消息，我们的科研团队没能成功地把那件文物从晶体石笋中取出。可能出于操作过于暴力，团队把这座支柱彻底砸碎了。更糟糕的是，其中的文物被损坏到无法辨认，而整间石室里充盈的灵能霎时消失无踪。

所幸这些晶体本身还是颇具价值的。即使我们也许永远无法完全了解这个先驱文明修建这个场所的目的，我们的努力至少没有完完全全白费。
descriptions.en:
Frustration on [From.Planet.GetName] as our science team has failed to remove the artifact from the crystal stalagmite. Perhaps working with too much vigor, the team's efforts caused the pillar to shatter. Worse, the artifact within was damaged beyond recognition, and all traces of psionic energy have vanished from the chamber.

One minor consolation is that the crystal itself could prove extremely valuable. While we may never fully understand the intentions of the precursor civilization that built this place, at least our efforts have not entirely been in vain.

descriptions.zh:
在[From.Planet.GetName]的科学团队有了新的突破！他们小心地将晶体支柱完整地挖掘了出来。其中保存着一个古老的、类人的面具。它的里侧写着一些象形文字，指明这件文物的名字叫做“造化之面具”。这些字符可能会意自这颗行星的卫星所具有的转变性的力量，即随着月相的变化操控潮涨潮落。

面具本身则具有难以置信的灵能性质，很有可能就是这颗行星发生快速气候变化的原因。无论是谁培养了那座晶体支柱，以及谁精心种植了那些复杂的林冠地图，他们很显然都是出自崇拜并保护这件文物的目的。团队提出的理论是，如果运用得当，这个面具可以协助我们的帝国转变整颗行星。
descriptions.en:
A breakthrough from the science team on [From.Planet.GetName]! Their careful excavation of the crystal pillar is complete. Preserved within was an ancient, humanoid mask. Ideographs on the reverse side refer to the artifact as The Mask of Transformation. This is likely a reference to the transformative power of the planet's moon, controlling the tides as it transitions from one phase to the next.

The Mask itself possesses incredible psionic properties, and is likely responsible for the rapid climatological transformation of the planet. Whoever fostered the crystal pillar and planted the elaborate map of trees in the forest above clearly intended to honor and protect this artifact. The team theorizes that, if properly used, the Mask may enable our empire to transform entire worlds.

descriptions.zh:
正如我们预期，这艘“恒星帆船”的内部相当古色古香。它的舰桥甚至仍是仿照古时候在行星液态海面上航行的那种帆船进行设计的。

甲板的材料似乎是金属，但大部分表面又以雕刻的木材覆盖，而观察窗和数据显示屏又是以类似玻璃的材料制成。

将舰船的计算机通电后，我们发现了一首老式的航海家之歌的数据文件。据我们的考古学家称，这种旋律曾一度被称为“船歌”或者“太空船歌”。我们目前正在尝试翻译歌词。
descriptions.en:
As we expected, the interior of this 'solar sailer' is appropriately archaic. The bridge resembles the deck of an old planetbound sailing ship designed to sail on watery seas.

The deck plating appears to be metal, but most surfaces are covered with carved wood, a contrast to the glass-like substance on viewports and datascreens.

Powering up the ship's computers, we have found a datafile with an old-fashioned seafarers' song. According to our archaeologist, this melody was once known as a 'sea chanty' or 'space shanty.' We are attempting to transcribe the lyrics.

descriptions.zh:
在我们完成对数据文件的修复和重新激活后，很快一首敲击节拍的音乐旋律充盈起了整艘舰船，伴随着一个自动调音过后的古代航海家的歌声。歌词大意：

“来啊，航行太空的年轻小伙子们，请听吧！
我要唱一首畅游于大海的鱼之歌！

小伙子们，狂风将起，风暴将临
当大风吹起，我们就出航吧！
大风向远方吹吧，嘿！快吹吧！
向着星海，她缓缓启航。

恒星风骤起，
带我向远方。
穿过那太空航道，
我们驶向星光！

小伙子们，狂风将起，风暴将临
当大风吹起，我们就出航吧！
大风向远方吹吧，嘿！快吹吧！
向着星海，她缓缓启航。”
descriptions.en:
Immediately after we completed the restoration and reactivation of the datafiles, a thrumming musical cadence surged throughout the ship, accompanied by the auto-tuned voices of ancient mariners. Transcription follows:

'Come all you young spacefarers, listen to me!
I'll sing you a song of our fish from the sea!

And it's windy weather, boys, stormy weather, boys
When the wind blows, then we're all together, boys
Blow ye winds fringeward, hey! Blow ye winds, blow!
Out to the galaxy, steady she goes.

Up come the solar winds
Taking us far
All through the space lanes
And out to the stars!

And it's windy weather, boys, stormy weather, boys
When the wind blows, then we're all together, boys
Blow ye winds fringeward, hey! Blow ye winds, blow!
Out to the galaxy, steady she goes!

descriptions.zh:
在我们探索这艘舰船的过程中，进一步的重新充能和对数据文件的恢复解锁了这首远古太空船歌的更多章节。这艘船的全息投影显示出水手、航海家们一起载歌载舞的扭曲抽动的影像：

“巨龙忽降临
寻找着我们的家乡
越过茫茫太空
找到波涛下的那个地方！

小伙子们，狂风将起，风暴将临
当大风吹起，我们就出航吧！
大风向远方吹吧，嘿！快吹吧！
向着星海，她缓缓启航。

缇扬奇跃起
它是深空之王
在这超空间竞速中
与我们的舰船互不相让

（合唱重复）

星神兽出现了！
它伸出触手
扼住了我们的舰船
我们惊恐万状！”
descriptions.en:
As we explored the ship, further attempts to power it up and recover its datafiles unlocked more stanzas of the ancient space shanty. The ship's holographic display vibrantly projected images of sailors and spacefarers singing and dancing in accompaniment:

'Up comes the Great Dragon
In search of our home
Through space to a place that's
Beneath waves and foam!

'And it's windy weather, boys, stormy weather, boys
When the wind blows, then we're all together, boys
Blow ye winds fringeward, hey! Blow ye winds, blow!
Out to the galaxy, steady she goes.

'Up comes the Tiyanki
The king of deep space
Racing our ships
In a hyperspace chase!

(chorus repeats)

'Up comes Leviathan
Tentacles grasp
Choking our ship
As we shiver and gasp!

(chorus repeats)

descriptions.zh:
我们的考古学家发现了一处可能是饮料的贮藏点。那些水手们喝的就是这种臭不可闻的液体么？我们肯定是不会喝这些奇怪的液体的。但我们对这艘船的探索成果着实令人沉醉！

“石质人来了
他们从巨岩中诞生
当他们聚到一起
这些巨砾将强壮无比！

（合唱）

死灵族来了
恐怖而又高大
你怎么都杀不死他们，伙计
他们还能复活！

（合唱）

机器蜂群来了
大家快跑吧
你得打一个、十个、一百个
1101！

（合唱）”
descriptions.en:
Our archaeologists have unearthed of a stash of potent potables. Were the sailors consuming these foul fluids? We will not ingest these strange liquids. Our exploration of the ship is already sufficiently intoxicating!

'Up come the Lithoids
All hewn from their stone
These boulders are bolder
When they're not alone!

(chorus)

'Up come the Necroids
All fearsome and great
You can't kill them, mateys,
They'll reanimate!

(chorus)

'Up come swarms of robots
Get ready to run
Fight one, ten, a dozen,
1101!

(chorus)

descriptions.zh:
我们的探索人员发现了远古历史的一隅，向世人展现了古代探险家们的热血和勇敢。显然，船长使用这首“太空船歌”来激励船员、协调行动。甚至他们独处的时候都喜欢唱这首歌！我们的考古学家认为，这部作品应当保存到博物馆当中。

至于这支古老的歌曲，我们已经翻译了能找到的全部歌词，并存入了我们的数据库。我们的“水手”甚至从中获取灵感，唱起了我们自己版本的太空船歌，这也能大大激发他们的士气和效率。

“我们生于深海
直抵苍穹
我们建设家园
直到永久！

小伙子们，狂风将起，风暴将临
当大风吹起，我们就出航吧！
大风向远方吹吧，嘿！快吹吧！
向着星海，她缓缓启航。”

现在是时候从这艘古老舰船中离开了，“抛开锚链”，借助恒星风扬帆起航。我们的大船将向着星海深处稳稳航行！
descriptions.en:
Our exploration has revealed a glance of ancient history, displaying the zeal and courage of ancient explorers. Clearly the captain used this 'space shanty' to motivate and coordinate the crew. Perhaps they even sang along! Our archaeologists are suggesting this performance should be preserved in a museum installation.

As for the ancient melody, we've transcribed all the lyrics we could find and added them to our databanks. Our own 'sailors' now have a habit of singing versions of their own space shanties, which should improve their morale and efficiency.

'We rose from the ocean
And reached for the sky
We're building an empire
That never will die!

'And it's windy weather, boys, stormy weather, boys
When the wind blows, then we're all together, boys
Blow ye winds fringeward, hey! Blow ye winds, blow
Out to the galaxy, steady she goes!'

It's time to untether from this ancient vessel, 'casting off the hawser' as we set sail on solar winds. Steady as she goes!
